Instead, after all the brothers of that monastery have been gathered together, they shall, by common agreement and through God’s providence, appoint as abbot from their own congregation the man who appears worthy of this honour.

But if anyone—which we do not desire—should attempt with reckless boldness to oppose what has been piously and firmly established by this authority of ours through this privilege, or should presume to resist or in any way transgress what we have established for the praise of God and the stability of the aforesaid monastery, let him know that he is bound by the chain of anathema by the authority of the blessed apostle Peter and is to be burned with the devil, his most dreadful pomp, and Judas, the betrayer of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the punishment of everlasting fire—unless he worthily corrects the evil he has committed.

But may he who, moved by pious concern, has been the guardian and observant keeper of this apostolic privilege obtain from our most merciful Judge, the Lord, the grace of confirmation and blessing, and eternal life with all God’s elect, for ever and ever. Amen.

Given on the eighth day before the Ides of August, by the hand of Peter, deacon, librarian and chancellor of the Holy Apostolic See, in the second year of the lord Pope Leo IX, indiction 4.

### XLIII. Saint Leo IX undertakes the protection of the monastery of Saint Victor of Marseille, at the request of Abbot Peter in the synod of Vercelli, and grants it the abbey of Saint Victor of Valence. (Year 1050.)

[Mansi, *Councils*, XIX, 779.]

[Col. 0652C]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Peter, abbot of the monastery of Saint Victor of Marseille, martyr and of all the apostles, and to your successors, the abbots: perpetual salvation in the Lord.

It is fitting for apostolic governance to assist with kindly compassion those who abound in pious religion and to grant suitable aid to the desires of petitioners. For from this the Creator of all things, God, will bestow the most excellent reward in the heavenly assemblies, if, with God’s help, venerable places are brought in our time to better observance and protected from the injury of wicked people.

Since, then, beloved son, when you came to our synod at Vercelli, you humbly and devoutly asked us for the protection of our apostolic defence and for a privilege for your monastery, which properly belongs to Saint Peter, we have inclined to your prayers. Through the terms of this apostolic command of ours, we decree by our apostolic authority that the aforesaid monastery of Saint Victor, martyr and of all the apostles, over which you have been deemed worthy to preside, shall always remain free from every human condition and yoke, since, being placed under the jurisdiction of Saint Peter, it has deserved to obtain liberty.

Moreover, we forbid anyone with a sacrilegious hand to dare to commit any molestation, violence, or plunder against the property of that monastery or its cells.

We also grant to your monastery a certain small abbey named Saint Victor, situated near the city of Valence. At the synod itself, Pontius, the bishop of that city, returned it to us with his own hands and completely renounced it; it had previously been unjustly held by the abbot of Saint Theodofred from the time of the devastation of the monastery of Saint Victor.

By apostolic censure we establish that no human person, whatever his power or condition, sex or age, shall ever attempt to act against this defence of our apostolic authority. If anyone dares to do so, he shall be pierced by the spear-point of anathema until he offers worthy satisfaction. But whoever guards himself against such presumption shall obtain the blessing of the Lord God and become a sharer in eternal life.

Given on the seventh day before the Ides of September, by the hand of Peter, deacon, librarian and chancellor of the Holy Apostolic See, in the year of the Lord 1050, the second year of Pope Leo IX, indiction 4.

### XLIV. He commends the monastery of Romainmoutier to [Henry], emperor of the Romans and king of the Burgundians, and to the bishops and princes of that region. (Year 1050.)

[*Memoirs and Documents of the Historical Society of Switzerland*, p. 419.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of the Lord, to H., his most beloved son, emperor of the Romans and king of the Burgundians, and to the bishops and princes of that region: greeting and apostolic blessing.

I wish your lordship and your successors to know that the monastery called Romainmoutier was once entrusted to our predecessors for preservation, guardianship, and protection—not for giving or selling, nor for granting as a benefice. I have wished to tell you briefly on what occasion this occurred.

I learned from the report of many people that the venerable lord Stephen, bishop of this Roman See, being hindered by certain necessities and gravely harassed by the Lombards, had to seek counsel from the king of the Franks. At that time the Roman world lacked an imperial figure, and those who appeared to be consuls and dictators were not of such strength that they could free the Holy Roman Church from so many storms threatening it.

At that time there was in the regions of Gaul a pious king named Pippin—the same Pippin whose son Charlemagne was his heir and imitator. When he heard of the necessity of the Holy Roman Church, he summoned the aforesaid lord Pope Stephen to come to him and to bring with him three princes, with whom he might find a wide-ranging plan for assisting his Church.

The pope consented to the king’s requests and came as far as Paris. The king and the princes of the kingdom received him honourably as supreme pontiff. The king treated him with such honour and reverence as was fitting for both of them, and kept him with him for a long time. In that place the Lord deigned to perform many miracles through him.

To say nothing of the rest, as the books of that monastery—Romainmoutier, or “Roman Monastery”—relate, he appeared to see the presence of the apostles Peter and Paul and of the blessed martyrs resting there, and to hear them addressing him, so that he might exalt that church by the authority of the apostles, choose and consecrate the aforesaid king P. and his sons as kings, and command by divine and apostolic authority that, throughout succeeding ages, no mortal should dare to appoint a king in that kingdom except from their lineage and descent.

In the course of the aforesaid business and journey, when he reached the monastery situated in certain parts of the Jura, he ordered lodging to be prepared for him. But once received and having enjoyed the service of the inhabitants, he, being pious and merciful, kindly accepted their hospitality. Out of charity he blessed and sanctified the place, consecrated churches there in honour of the apostles, and named it Romainmoutier.

That place, as we have heard, was later abandoned because of wicked men and troublesome neighbours. But, with the Lord’s consent, it was entrusted by King Conrad and his most noble wife Matilda, of blessed memory, to Maiolus and his successors, the monks; through their efforts it was restored and brought to secular honour and monastic religion. May that arrangement of blessed Maiolus and of the king and queen remain fixed and stable.

Furthermore, I wish the property always to remain subject to us, so that if anyone there commits an injury, hears a complaint from us and our successors, and refuses to make amends, he may know fully that he will be excommunicated by apostolic authority.

### XLV. Saint Leo IX confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Saint Mansuetus. (Year 1030.)

[Dom Calmet, *History of Lorraine*, I, Proofs, 429.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Dodo, beloved son in Christ, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mansuetus, situated in the suburb of our city of Toul, and to his successors, who are to be regularly promoted in the future.

Just as a petition contrary to reason must be rejected, so it is not fitting to deny fulfilment to things that are rightly desired. Therefore, agreeing to your prayers, dearest son in Christ, and seeking the perpetual peace and stability of your monastery, we have decreed by the stability of this present decree that neither a bishop nor any other person shall have the right to exercise in it any burden or harassment, or in any way, through any exaction, to diminish its revenues, property, or charters, its villages or cells, or anything belonging to it; nor shall anyone presume to devise any fraud or intrusion, as is contained in the charters of the blessed Gerard and in the ancient privileges of that place.

So that the brothers serving God there may devote themselves more freely to their duties, let them possess free and undisturbed from every secular ban, and exempt from every exaction, the entire estate on which that monastery is situated, and whatever they justly possess today or may possess in the future within the parish, according to the boundaries described in the charter of the aforesaid bishop.

We also confirm to you the cell at Moyen-Vic, the cell of Mount Bar, with its parish, the church of Germaio, the church of Boneio with the chapel of Ornezons, the church of Godelincourt, the church of Parneio, the church of Bladiniaco, the church of Marceio, the church of Tulliacum, the church of Purnes, the church of Boverons, the church of Andeliers, the church of Serto, and the church of Limeis, with all your appurtenances, altars, and tithes. No person shall in any way be permitted to diminish or take away anything from the aforesaid possessions, nor shall anyone dare to construct a church or chapel within the aforesaid boundaries.

Likewise, we confirm to you all your villages, namely Angeriacum, with its complete fishery in every use and under every ban; Molosiacum; Sessiacum; and the other Sessiacum, with its forest and ban; Tulliacum; Sartum, with its forest and ban; the estate of Gibonis; Purnes; and Germaium, with its forest and ban, together with all male and female unfree persons belonging to the aforesaid villages.

Moreover, whatever that monastery justly possesses today, or may justly and canonically acquire in the future through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors.

Therefore we decree that absolutely no one shall rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations. Rather, everything granted for their appropriate support and governance shall be preserved intact and shall in every way contribute to their uses.

If, however, any prince, priest, judge, or secular person, recognizing this page of our constitution, attempts to act against it, let him irrecoverably lose the dignity of his power and rank, and let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed. Unless he either restores what he has wrongly taken away or mourns it after performing worthy penance for the unlawful act, let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment let him be subjected to strict vengeance.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who rightly preserve what belongs to that place, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. Amen. Amen. Amen.

+ I, Leo, bishop of the Catholic Church, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1050, indiction 4.

Given at Toul, in the greater church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of November, by the hand of Udo, primicerius, chancellor and librarian of our Church of Toul and of the Holy Apostolic See, in the second year of the apostolate of the lord Pope Leo IX, the twenty-sixth year of the episcopate of Toul.

### XLVI. Saint Leo IX confirms the privileges of the canons of the church of Saint Stephen of Toul. (Year 1050.)

[Dom Calmet, *History of Lorraine*, I, Proofs, p. 435.]

[Col. 0656A]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the most beloved Church of Toul of the glorious protomartyr Stephen, and through it to the dearest sons who perpetually serve God there: perpetual salvation in the Lord.

If we give assistance to those who serve the interests of Holy Mother Church, we confidently hope that this will certainly increase our salvation through the gift of heavenly recompense. And when their holy devotion is more fervently increased by us for divine worship, we trust that the eternal Judge will grant us no small share in the reward due to them.

Therefore let it be known to all the faithful of Christ, present and future, that while we were residing at Vercelli in an apostolic synod for the sake of the state of divine religion, Udo, primicerius of the Holy Church of Toul—from which we were elected to this apostolic burden, not through our merits but through the call of divine grace—and which we still held under the ordering of our entire oversight, came into our presence with many other devout servants of God.

He entreated us to strengthen, by confirmation of our authority, the privilege of the villages, churches, various properties, and also vineyards lying in every place, belonging to the uses of the canons serving God, Holy Mary his mother, and the blessed protomartyr Stephen. We fulfilled his petition in every respect with fatherly care.

Then, eagerly desiring to visit that same Church of Toul and wishing with a heart full of fatherly charity to embrace its most beloved flock—which we had left desolate, namely, its clergy and people—we came to that church, especially because divine admonition urged us to transfer from the tomb the glorious body of our most holy predecessor and confessor Gerard. When the desire of so great a longing had been fulfilled, we arrived there and, by God’s grace, transferred the body of our glorious confessor Gerard. For the praise and glory of Almighty God and of all the faithful of Christ, we magnified him as was worthy and just, in accordance with what was fitting for human and apostolic authority.

[Col. 0656D] While we were still present and investigating various matters for the support of the church, we discovered with manifest truth that certain non-ministerials were, through hidden evasions, gnawing away at certain chapters from the privilege of the blessed Gerard and from ours. Convicted by judgment, they could not proceed, since the case, supported by the testimony and judgment of Count Rainard and of other truthful lords of the city, prevailed.

Through these men the church also respectfully appealed to our apostolic dignity and urgently requested that the same privilege be confirmed by us. We satisfied the petition of the brothers before the great multitude that had gathered for the solemn translation of the glorious confessor, with the full counsel of the entire church concerning the estates and with the judgment of the faithful lords of the city. The following letter will serve as evidence concerning these matters.

For the increase of our reward before God, we confirm to you, brothers of the Holy Church of Toul, your dwellings within and outside the city, free from every ban and secular jurisdiction. From now on neither your bishop, nor the counts of Toul, nor a duke, nor any secular authority shall demand from your villages an advocacy, service, or any due. The emperors and kings, and the glorious holy confessor Gerard, after the truth had been recognized, left these entirely under your control and free under anathema until our time.

Likewise, we leave and confirm to your uses, excluding every secular power and without any voice of contradiction, the vineyards, lands, estates, people of either sex, and all property situated or lying anywhere.

If it should happen that your people, whatever their sex, leave your villages, no person and no ban shall be permitted to retain them as his own. Nor shall this be done to their descendants wherever they may be, as is commonly called “beautiful reinvestiture” (*belle reinvestitura*). Wherever they go, you shall be permitted to possess them freely as before.

Your cloistered steward shall choose one of your men to guard the vineyards of Bar and shall assign him that guardianship. Then he shall present him to the city steward only to swear fidelity. In all the jurisdictions in which by ancient right you receive the episcopal demesne tithes, you shall have one man, free from the ban, with his census and estate, just as Saint Gerard instituted, to guard the tithes; and if he dies, you shall take another from the same jurisdiction.

We also confirm one estate at Paterniacum, entirely free, with all its appurtenances and with all the other things in that village, having freely the full use of both pastures and roads and paths. We also confirm the fishing ban on the Moselle, beginning upstream at the rock of the mill of Saint Aper and Saint Vedastus and extending to the stream flowing down from the summit of the mountain called Castellum, so that no person may fish there under any ban without your permission.

We further confirm half of the church, together with the provision for its vicar, in the village of Totonis, which the venerable bishop Gauzelinus gave to you for the commemoration of his anniversary.

Your people residing within or outside the city shall have the common use of the city ban with all the others, and shall be subject to no secular jurisdiction except yours—apart from external commerce, if they have been enrolled by the city steward among the other merchants subject to the ban.

If you should lack kitchen or bakery servants for the service of the cloister, you shall be permitted to take suitable persons from the court of your bishop, or from any monastery in the city or diocese, if suitable people for your cloistered service are found there.

All the foregoing we confirm to you, brothers, by apostolic censure and under divine adjuration, so that no emperor, duke, count, secular person, archbishop, bishop, or any other person, whatever his condition or profession, shall attempt to act against this constitution of ours. Whoever does so shall remain struck by our apostolic anathema until he offers worthy satisfaction. But whoever guards and observes it shall, through our blessing, become a sharer in eternal life. Amen.

Given at Toul, in the greater church, by the hand of Udo, primicerius, chancellor and librarian of the Church of Toul and of the Holy Apostolic See, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of November, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1051, indiction 4, in the second year of the apostolate of the lord Pope Leo IX.

### XLVII. Privilege of Saint Leo IX for Saint Hugh concerning the church of Raningas. (Year 1050.)

[*Cluniac Bullary*, 12.]

[Col. 0658B]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Hugh, venerable abbot of the monastery of Cluny, and to his successors for ever.

Since you asked us, dearest brother, to confirm by apostolic authority certain goods granted to our Church of Cluny by certain God-fearing men, through this page of our command we confirm them to you and your successors according to your petition, since we have found it reasonable and honourable.

Therefore, with the shield of our protection, we strengthen for the aforesaid monastery the church with the estate called Raningas, constructed as a cell. The good-memory Riquinus of Dorneio gave it to our aforesaid monastery with the consent of his wife, named Loanceda.

Namely, we confirm to you perpetually the estate of Raningas itself with all its appurtenances: cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, waters and watercourses, pastures, male and female servants, and everything that they are seen to possess there; also churches, male and female servants, and estates, just as they were written down by the aforesaid Riquinus, with the approval and consent of the bishop of the Church of Toul, while preserving the authority and honour of his Church.

We also confirm to you the estate that Hugh of Longa Aqua gave to Saint Peter of the Church of Cluny, which is the head of your cell.

Furthermore, whatever else was later granted to that place by good men, or was justly acquired, or may be acquired in the future, we likewise approve and confirm. By apostolic censure we establish that no king, archbishop, bishop, duke, count, viscount, or any other judicial person shall dare to bring any accusation against this page of our protection.

Whoever strives to preserve and guard it unharmed shall have our abundant blessing. But whoever acts against it, struck by the arrow of our anathema and lying in the death of his soul, shall never deserve to rise to eternal life unless he repents.

[Col. 0659A] Given on the seventh day before the Kalends of November, by the hand of Udo of Toul, primicerius, chancellor and librarian of the Holy Apostolic See, in the year of the lord Leo IX, indiction 4.

### XLVIII. Saint Leo IX confirms the possessions and rights of the monastery of Saint Vincent of Metz, at the request of Bishop Adalbero. (Year 1050.)

[Dom Calmet, *History of Lorraine*, I, Proofs, 437.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved fellow-bishop Adalbero, bishop of Metz.

By divine law we are admonished to rejoice with the just intention of God’s faithful and to become cooperators in their good will, so that through their holy work we may be able to share in the reward and fellowship of remuneration.

Therefore, dearest brother, we rejoice in your holy devotion and praise your worthy petition by apostolic authority, because you labour diligently so that the community of those serving God may always be enlarged and increased through you. Accordingly, we have decided to publish abundantly what you and Folchuinus, the abbot of your monastery of Saint Vincent the Martyr, request, and to confirm it through the authority of apostolic institution and the censure of privileges and decrees.

It is indeed fitting for apostolic governance to arrange appropriately, or certainly to bring to a better state, holy and venerable places that had long been in ruins and were living in great want and poverty—especially where those things are requested that concern not the temporal advantage of the petitioners but the perpetual provision for souls serving God.

Thus, the venerable place which your predecessor, Deoderic, bishop of Metz, gathered together and joined as one with its own communities—communities that regularly offer uninterrupted vigils in psalms, hymns, and prayers to God our Saviour Jesus Christ—may remain protected from external insolence and continually be able to offer the duties of pious service in the monastery of Saint Vincent.

Since it is clear that your religious devotion has asked us to confirm this privilege because of changes in temporal affairs and the varied fortunes of men, we have decreed that the protection of Saint Vincent the Martyr, together with everything belonging to that monastery, and the strengthening of that congregation in Christ and of its successors, shall be established perpetually.

Accordingly, a ninth of all the revenues of the bishopric, and one estate from each *curtis*, which were given to them by the aforesaid Deoderic and his successors, shall be preserved in the future until the end, just as you too laudably grant them.

And so that that congregation, remaining undisturbed and persevering as one, may be able to offer diligent praises to God and continue perpetually in the practices with which God has inspired them, let the aforesaid place, established in honour of Saint Vincent, remain under one abbot, undivided, and let the congregation remain undivided. Let no one be permitted, fleeing the rigour of the rule to which he has devoted himself, to wander hither and thither or attempt to move to other monasteries. This we prohibit under the bond of anathema, contrary to the rule.

Therefore, establishing and promulgating before God and before his terrible future judgment, through this page of our apostolic privilege and constitution we sanction, and by the authority of the blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, we decree and solemnly charge both future pontiffs of the Apostolic See and those who administer episcopal office, as well as every great or small person and anyone endowed with whatever dignity or power, that no one shall have permission in any way to separate or alienate from the often-mentioned place of Saint Vincent anything that was given and granted to that venerable place by the aforesaid Bishop Deoderic or by anyone else and possessed for thirty years by the monks serving God there.

And so that the monastery of Saint Vincent may look toward the episcopal seat of Christ’s protomartyr Stephen, we command it; and the abbot shall hold primacy so as to perform the functions of the bishop’s representative. If the bishop is absent, he shall also be permitted on feast days to go to the episcopal seat and celebrate Mass there wearing the dalmatic and sandals.

If anyone meanwhile—which we do not believe—should attempt with reckless boldness to oppose what has been piously and firmly arranged by this authority of ours through this privilege, or should presume to resist, take away, or alienate what the often-mentioned Deoderic, bishop of Metz, or anyone else established for the praise of God and the stability of the aforesaid monastery of Saint Vincent, and what those serving God there have possessed for thirty years, let him know that he is bound by the authority of the blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, with the bond of anathema, and that he is to be burned with Judas, the betrayer of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the punishment of everlasting fire. Thus condemned, let him never be released from the bonds of the aforesaid anathema.

But whoever, moved by pious concern, proves himself observant in all things shall receive from our most merciful Lord an abundant share of the grace of blessing, become a participant in eternal life, and have the chain of blessed Peter, given to him by the Holy Roman Church, open the gate of paradise for him. But if anyone diminishes anything belonging to it, let that chain close the kingdoms of heaven against him.

Moreover, dearest fellow-brother, since you ask that the cell of Caliniacum, where you have arranged a community of monks, attached as a dependent cell to the aforesaid monastery of Saint Vincent, be freed from the census which it has hitherto customarily paid to the Church of Toul, as do other chapels, we approve your request and establish it as free for ever, on the condition that the order of monastic religion be established there.

But if—which may it not happen—the community of monks there should disappear because of the fault of some superior, let the aforesaid census again be demanded by the bishop of the See of Toul according to customary practice.

And so that the things we have stated may, without any opposition, be ratified and firmly established, we have strengthened them by the firmness of our subscription and ordered them to be marked by the impression of our seal against the voices of all who might object.

Given at Toul on the fourth day before the Nones of November, by the hand of Udo of Toul, primicerius, chancellor and librarian of the Holy Apostolic See, in the year from the Incarnation of the Lord 1051, and in the second year of the lord Pope Leo IX, indiction 4.

### XLIX. Bull of Saint Leo IX for the monastery of Saints Bertarius and Atalenus. (Year 1030.)

[Mabillon, *Annals of the Order of Saint Benedict*, IV, 740.]

Leo, servant of the servants of God, to the church of the blessed martyrs Bertarius and Atalenus, which is called Bledericivilla and is situated in the county of Sante, and through it to the nuns who are to serve there perpetually: perpetual salvation in the Lord.

[Col. 0661B]

It is undoubtedly considered to belong to the care of our apostolate that venerable places should be fortified by our apostolic authority, and that what benefits them by strengthening their protection should contribute to our increase in salvation. Therefore it seemed equitable and salutary to us that we should fortify by the shield of apostolic authority the aforesaid church, founded by Count Raynard and his forebears, and decree that it remain in the monastic order.

Accordingly, by that authority through which, although unworthy, we nevertheless exercise on earth the office of the most blessed Apostle Peter, we confirm and strengthen, by this document of our apostolic privilege, in perpetuity for that holy and venerable place, everything granted or to be granted to it by the same Count Raynard, by his relatives, and by any other faithful Christians [Col. 0661C]. By our apostolic authority we prohibit that this place ever be removed from the monastic order; rather, let it always remain under the rule of Saint Benedict. In particular, we confirm the properties which Count Raynard himself gave to this place for the remedy of his soul, whose names we have caused to be written here: namely, the whole of Bledericivilla, with its church and all its appurtenances; Romaldusvilla, with all its appurtenances; Salsuris, with all its appurtenances; Pantevillare, with all its appurtenances; the allod of Lord Basolus; Ligisdicurtis, with all its appurtenances; and the allod of Unzoniscurtis.

After the most firm confirmation of these gifts [Col. 0661D], just as the aforesaid count had already requested, he asked that it be consecrated by us while we presided solely over the episcopate of Toul; indeed, it was consecrated. Thus now, elevated by divine mercy to the summit of the apostolate, we decree that henceforth a congregation of nuns be venerably established there for the praise of God and the veneration of the saints, and that it be confirmed under the protection of the blessed Mother and Virgin Mary and of Saint Stephen the Protomartyr, in the church of Toul. We stipulate that whoever from the descendants of his family lawfully possesses the castle of Fontenay shall securely hold the advocacy of this place.

But if, perhaps, no one survives from the line of his succession, let the aforesaid advocacy pass to the nearest and eldest person who descends from the stock of that Raynard, or from whose inheritance the place itself was founded [Col. 0662A]. Each year, on the Invention of Saint Stephen, the established congregation of that place shall pay the due census for its subjection, namely one wax candle valued at twelve Toul denarii.

The gift of the abbey shall always remain in the hand of the bishop of Toul. Whoever from the stock of the aforementioned count is found suitable in that monastery shall receive responsibility for the place under the title of abbess. But if no such person can be found there, a worthy woman from his descendants shall be taken from the place of Saint Romaric to become abbess. And if none can be found in either of these two monasteries, the bishop shall have the authority to seek, either from those places or from others within the episcopate of Toul, another worthy person and, according to God’s will, place her over that community.

Therefore, if anyone—which God forbid, and which we scarcely believe could happen—should attempt to disagree with this public enactment of ours, and, under the pretext of some payment, appoint a superior of the place contrary to the Lord’s will, or wish to destroy the place or diminish its dependencies, the advocate shall have free authority to approach the king, explain the monastery’s case there prudently, and strive with the utmost zeal to remedy the violation of this apostolic command.

But if the advocate should wish by force or malicious design to diminish anything from the monastery’s resources, or even to violate this apostolic confirmation of ours, then, if, after being warned twice and a third time by the bishop, he is willing to amend his fault justly, let the advocacy remain his. But if, against the bishop’s admonition or excommunication, he remains incorrigible, let him lose the advocacy, and let the bishop seek another advocate who will faithfully provide for the defense of the place.

And so that he may not presume to seize anything from the church’s dependencies, we decree that on the feast of the holy martyrs Bertarius and Atalenus he shall be given there a provision: one measure of grain, one measure of wine—or, if the wine is lacking, three solidi in the coinage of that district—and a two-year-old pig. In no way, however, shall he presume to interfere with the property or rights of the abbey, unless perhaps he has been summoned by the abbess for assistance; and then, for his presence and assistance, he shall receive a third part of the same abbey [Col. 0662D].

Moreover, so that the confirmation of this matter might be preserved more cautiously and firmly forever, only after the repeated and urgent requests of Lanhardis, daughter of the often-mentioned Count Raynard, and with the careful counsel of her faithful men—namely Richuinus and Cuno, as well as Rhindricus or Theobaldus—we have assigned similar privileges to both places: one, as seemed appropriate, to the holy Church of Toul, and the other to the aforesaid monastery. Through this most carefully secured privilege, neither shall the authority of the bishop of Toul be injured, nor shall any unjust disadvantage come from the bishop to the church’s servants of God.

By apostolic censure, under the invocation of divine judgment, we decree that no emperor, no king, no duke, no marquis, no count, no viscount, no advocate, no archbishop, no bishop, and, moreover, no person whatsoever, of whatever sex or age, shall attempt to act against this confirmation and constitution of our apostolic authority [Col. 0663A]. Whoever does so shall remain struck by our apostolic anathema until he has rendered worthy satisfaction. But upon whoever guards and observes this confirmation and constitution, may our blessing be multiplied, and may he be made a participant in eternal life.

Given on the eighth day before the Ides of December, through the hands of Udo, primicerius of Toul, chancellor and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the second year of Pope Lord Leo IX, indiction IV.

### L. Bull of Saint Leo IX concerning the consecration of the church of Hohenburg, performed by him himself. (Year 1050.)

[Gallia Christiana IV, 471, from the original preserved in the archive of the most serene prince-bishop of Strasbourg.]

[Col. 0663B]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the church of Mary, Mother of God, where rests the body of the holy virgin Odila, called Hohenburg, and through it to the nuns who will serve there perpetually: everlasting salvation in the Lord.

When we were visiting the regions of Alsace with pious regard, it happened that we came to Hohenburg. Since we rightly maintain constant concern for all churches, a benevolent devotion also intervened here, and the dutiful memory of our parents, who had always served there devotedly and rested in Christ, constrained us to dedicate as a dwelling for the Holy Spirit the aforesaid church, which we found as though uncultivated [Col. 0663C]. We did this as was fitting.

To this temple, dedicated in honor of the holy Mother of God and Saint Nicholas, the venerable abbess named Bertha, for the remedy of her soul and those of her parents, gave the estate with its dependents which she possessed at the place called Archenheim and at Meinholdesheim, Sahsenheim, Uresheim, and Gersheim.

Furthermore, we decree that at the two altars—one of which is at the head of blessed Odila, and the other in the principal church—no one shall celebrate the solemnities of Mass except the bishop of that diocese and suitable weekly priests of that church. In addition, any suitable person who comes may celebrate, but not without the consent and permission of the prelate of the place or of the congregation, if she herself is not present [Col. 0663D].

Moreover, a religious priest shall be provided daily to minister at the altar of Saint Odila; he shall also worthily perform the office of chaplain in the service of the prelate. Since it accords with our apostolic governance to assist with benevolent compassion those distinguished by pious religion, just as is contained in the privileges of our predecessors, so it seemed appropriate to us to grant a fitting assent to the desires of the church and of the nuns serving God there.

Therefore, by this stable privilege of our authority we grant and confirm, decreeing by apostolic censure and under the invocation of divine judgment that the aforesaid church shall possess the aforesaid estate inviolably, and that no one may diminish or take away anything from the properties granted to it by the founders or by other faithful Christians. These include Rodsheim, Torolsesheim, Avelsheim, Sahselsheim, Bladensheim, Scafersheim, Ehenheim, Renchirchen, Ingemarsheim, Ehenheim, Egensheim, Sigoliesheim, Alege, Sunthusen, Argensheim, Scopfheim, Gersheim, Bercheim, Tullengen, the Salic land at Saint Nabor, and whatever is to be granted. Rather, everything shall remain wholly intact for the nuns serving God there [Col. 0664A].

We have also decreed that whenever an abbess of that place dies, the nuns shall have the power to elect without disagreement an abbess who will lawfully preside over them. We command that, if they can find among their own number a woman who is worthy and religious, they elect her without anyone’s opposition [Col. 0664B]. Otherwise, let them choose the best one they can find, and bring the elected woman to the bishop for consecration; she shall also have her subjects consecrated by the bishop in their order.

For the entire area of the mountain, which, as we have learned from ancient tradition, was possessed solely by spiritual persons in the time of blessed Odila, we have likewise decreed shall be subject to the aforesaid abbess. Namely, no human being shall dare to cultivate or possess any part of that mountain within the boundaries of the pagan wall without the abbess’s permission, and no one shall presume by any disturbance to violate the peace which we have perpetually imposed upon those places [Col. 0664C].

Furthermore, we decree that no one, whatever his power or condition, shall dare to exact anything from the aforesaid church by force or violence. Rather, let it always remain tranquil and secure in divine praises.

The abbess herself shall in no way squander the monastery’s goods through unjust freedom. As the faithful steward of the supreme Emperor, she shall diligently gather and prudently guard everything that will benefit the poor of Christ and the church’s needs, not the vanity of the world, so that the sheep of Christ, whom she must feed spiritually and bodily, do not lack temporal pastures and may more freely seek and find eternal ones.

If she does not do this, and, after being warned once, twice, or three times, remains incorrigible, let her be canonically deposed by judicial sentence before the Church, and let a more useful person be placed in her stead.

Therefore, by that authority through which we exercise the office of Saint Peter, we irrevocably confirm that no emperor, no king, no archbishop [Col. 0664D], and no other person, great or small, shall attempt in any way to act against this confirmation. Whoever does so shall be struck by our apostolic anathema until he humbly repents. But whoever guards it shall become a participant in eternal life.

Let anyone who dares to burden the church of Hohenburg through contention or rebellion also be struck by the same anathema, if he is one of the weekly priests. The weekly priests themselves shall possess nothing on the mountain except the necessary houses granted to them by the abbess as a benefice. Amen.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January, through the hands of Udo of Toul, primicerius, chancellor and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the second year of Pope Lord Leo IX, indiction IV.

### LI. Privilege granted by Saint Leo IX to the canons of Agaunum. (Year 1050.)

[Gallia Christiana, vol. XII, p. 427.]

[Col. 0665A]

In the fear of the eternal God and of our Savior Jesus Christ, Leo, the most humble servant of the servants of God, elevated to the height of the apostolic dignity—not by his own merits, but by the divine assistance of the heavenly key-bearer and chief of the other apostles, Peter.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, in order to free the human race from the guilt of the first parent, descended from heaven to earth and entrusted to blessed Peter, redeemed by his own blood, the task of feeding it. Through the succession of this ministry, it has reached us, although unworthy [Col. 0665B]. Therefore all Christians ought to hasten to the holy mother Church and to the apostolic see, so that the Founder may obtain the fruit of devotion and that assistance may not be denied to the pious construction of a sanctuary through the granting of privileges.

We wish it to be known to all the sons of the universal Church that, while we were traveling through the regions of Gaul to raise up the Church that was shipwrecked in those parts of the world, we came to the place called Agaunum, which the precious martyrs Mauritius and his fellow soldiers drenched with their blood. Although we remained there for three days and, through apostolic privileges, found that holy and wealthy place adorned with patronage, nevertheless we saw it deprived of every treasure and of the fullness of its benefits. We consoled it as best we could, and finally celebrated the feasts of those martyrs [Col. 0665C].

While our archdeacon Peter was present with us, together with the bishops Allinard of Lyon, Hugh of Besançon, Frederick of Geneva, and Aymo of Sion, who now presides over that church, we were informed—among the other matters reported to us—of the mournful burden of afflictions imposed upon the canons of that place, although this had previously been prohibited by the authority of a privilege. The canons were not permitted at the end of life to distribute their own goods, nor while alive to dispose of anything from the church’s property without the will of their superior.

We ordered the aforesaid bishops, and especially that bishop, namely Aymo, their superior, to communicate this unheard-of offense to Emperor Henry, who was to meet us at Cologne, so that with his counsel and assistance we might calm the ruin caused by such violence. Having heard not only then but many times their tearful complaint, the most pious Emperor Henry asked us to adorn with the privilege and insignia of the apostolic see the same monastery of Agaunum, in which Aymo is known to be abbot under the rule of the canons. Under the holy Church over which, by God’s authority, we preside, he asked us to honor by the dignity of our pontificate the order established by former kings—most gloriously by King Sigismund and by the other kings after him—and the statutes and privileges of that monastery, so that they might never be corrupted [Col. 0665D].

Thus no superior might be imposed over those canons without their common counsel or election; nothing might be undertaken concerning the church’s common property after their proper disposition of it; and the violence of the aforesaid persons might not prevail by rashly seizing their private or common goods. Rather, everything should be ordered according to their decrees and by the authority of the privilege [Col. 0666A].

And if one of them should be unexpectedly overtaken by death, when he has no parents, let them distribute his goods to the Church, the household, and the poor as they know to be proper. So that no superior, by exercising any authority there, might disturb their voice of joy, we bind him under the bond of anathema.

We also restore to them in the episcopate of Lausanne a certain estate called Auronum, formerly taken from them by the violence of superiors, together with its churches and remaining dependencies, so that it may always serve the brothers’ table [Col. 0666B].

Therefore, lending an ear to the pious prayers of the brothers, and to the congregation of the aforesaid monastery, which adheres to the divine commandments and observes the rule of the apostolic see, we commit to effect, through the authority of this command of ours, what they request.

Accordingly, we permit no priest of any church to hold episcopal or prior jurisdiction in the aforesaid monastery or in the churches situated on its estates. We prohibit anyone who holds the city of Sion, in the name of Valais, from claiming any jurisdiction or power there except by the authority of the apostolic see. Unless invited by the prelate of the church or by the brothers, no one shall presume to come there to celebrate the mysteries of Mass or to exercise his domination; nor shall anyone put forward any unauthorized assemblies or claim a share in the alms granted to Saint Maurice.

Nor shall anyone attempt to take away the tithes granted there by Saint Sigismund or by others, since they stand under the protection of the apostolic privilege. We decree through this document of our decree that everything shall remain unshaken at all times according to the wishes of its founder [Col. 0666C].

We also prohibit all persons endowed with whatever dignity, and bind them under the bond of anathema, if anyone should wish at any time or in any manner to corrupt the provisions of this institution, or the sanctions of the documents themselves concerning money and the privilege of liberty, which have been established by kings or other faithful persons and granted to the aforesaid monastery under privileges [Col. 0666D].

I, Leo, by the will of God, rereading this series of the privilege made by me for the love of God and in honor of the holy martyrs, have signed it, and ordered the bishops listed below to sign.

Peter, a sinner, signed at the command of the lord pope.

Gregory, a sinner, signed at the command of the lord pope.

Hugh, a sinner, signed at the command of the lord pope.

Herman, a sinner, signed at the command of the lord pope.

### LII. Saint Leo IX confirms the possessions of the church of Saints Martin and Agericus of Verdun, at the request of Bishop Theodoric. (Year 1051.)

[Dom Calmet, *History of Lorraine*, I, Documents, 441.]

[Col. 0667A]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the church of the holy confessors Martin and Agericus, and through it to Abbot Balderic, his successors, and their monks who will serve God there perpetually: eternal salvation in the Lord.

It is fitting for apostolic governance to provide prudently and wisely in all things for ecclesiastical honor, lest, if—God forbid—the negligence of the supreme pontiff should come first, the flock and pastures of other shepherds, inclined toward worse rather than better things, be badly managed [Col. 0667B].

Therefore, at the prayers of Theodoric, bishop of Verdun, the aforesaid abbot of good conduct, a faithful provider for his church, came to us with sufficient humility and propriety, requested this privilege of our apostolic authority, and obtained it.

Accordingly, with assent granted to a just petition, we confirm by this sacred page of our apostolic confirmation and decree that all the goods granted or ever to be granted to the aforesaid church by any faithful Christians, and especially those which, without anyone’s opposition and with entirely free authority, the bishop of Verdun, Rambert of blessed memory, granted—goods concerning which he had begun to arrange a permanent exchange at the monastery of Saint Paul situated in the same city—which his venerable successor Richard, out of love for God and in memory of his predecessor, who began that church of monks and completed it with God’s mercy, also confirmed, shall remain firm [Col. 0667C].

Furthermore, by the sacred authority of the first see we command and prohibit that any emperor, king, duke, marquis, count, viscount, advocate, archbishop, bishop, or any person, great or small, of ecclesiastical rank or worldly condition, dare rise against this constitution or confirmation.

But if anyone, fearing neither future harm to his soul nor taking precautions for his salvation, should carelessly incur guilt by violating this privilege [Col. 0667D] or perversely altering it, let him know that, unless he quickly repents, he has immediately been struck by the incurable dart of divine anathema. But whoever observes our salutary commands and counsels with due submission and humility beneficial to himself shall be enriched with the favorable advantage of salvation and with the gift of apostolic blessing.

Thus signed and subscribed: “The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord. Leo the Pope.”

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of January, through the hand of Udo, primicerius of the church of Toul and chancellor and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the third year of Pope Lord Leo IX [Note: [Col. 0667D] Read: second year. Jaffé], indiction IV.

### LIII. Saint Leo IX confirms the goods of the church of Besançon at the request of Archbishop Hugh and grants it certain privileges. (Year 1051.)

[Dunod, *History of the Church of Besançon*, I, Documents, p. 36.]

[Col. 0668A]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Hugh, archbishop of the holy Chrysopolitan Church, and to his successors forever.

We give thanks to God and our Lord Jesus Christ, who, although we had no preceding merits of our own, nevertheless raised us to the summit of the apostolic see. Therefore it seems to belong to the care of our apostolate to maintain concern for all churches and to increase their honor [Col. 0668B].

Since you requested from the Roman see, most blessed brother, that the goods which the mercy of the Almighty has brought about in your time for the Church divinely entrusted to you should be fortified by our authority, it pleased us to consent to your petition according to your desire. In particular, the sacred place over which, by God’s arrangement, you appear to preside shines with such dignity that it is elevated not only by the authority of an archiepiscopal see but also remains distinguished, with due reverence for its equity, by the privileges of many apostolic fathers.

Our joy in its greater title also invites us to this, because the aforesaid place is adorned by the patronage of the protomartyr Stephen, whose priceless relic of the arm it preserves, a much-desired gift. To speak more truly, we saw with our own eyes the bone of that most sacred relic, battered by the blows of the Jews who stoned him, when we placed it inside the altar that we consecrated in your presence [Col. 0668C].

Our fellow bishops were present: Alinard, archbishop of Lyon; George, archbishop of the Colosensis church of the Hungarians; Kilinus, bishop of Sutri; Frederick of Geneva; Wido of Chalon; and Walter of Mâcon. Also present were abbots and honorable clerics of revered sanctity, together with an immense multitude of laypeople. In the course of your prayers you added that, since the altar had been consecrated by our hands, it should receive some dignity from the apostolic see.

Therefore, moved by your just prayers, we did not delay in offering you an ascent of piety [Col. 0668D]. Accordingly, by this document of our command we confirm all the goods granted either through your efforts or through the devotion of any faithful persons.

Finally, in honor of our protomartyr, we decree that Mass be celebrated only once a day upon the aforesaid holy altar. No one shall presume to approach it to offer the sacrifice except one whom the archbishop of the place has appointed for this purpose with the consent of the brothers—namely, seven brothers of that congregation, chosen for the excellence of their life and called cardinals. One of them shall be dean of that church; and just as he is senior in the congregation, so shall he excel in dignity.

Whoever among these celebrates Mass there shall wear a dalmatic, and only then dare to celebrate with all reverence and religious observance. They shall also use sandals and a mitre—the priest himself, the deacon, and the subdeacon—on the feasts of the Lord and our Savior, of the blessed Mother of God, and of the archangel Saint Michael; on the feast days of the apostles and of the holy martyrs Stephen, Vincent, and Agapitus, whose head we placed with the arm of Saint Stephen in the same altar; of the blessed Ferreolus and Ferrucius; on the feast of All Saints; and on the dedication of that place.

We likewise deny this privilege to all bishops and abbots, unless perhaps they have been invited. By apostolic censure we decree that no one of ecclesiastical rank shall dare violate any of these provisions.

We confirm by our apostolic protection that no emperor, king [Col. 0669B], duke, count, viscount, archbishop, bishop, or power of any order shall dare act against this shield of apostolic defense, diminish anything from the church’s goods belonging to the brothers’ prebend, or give any of them as a benefice to anyone.

If anyone declares that any of the goods possessed by the church is subject to litigation, no one shall be permitted to seize it before the matter has been judicially determined. But if anyone should rashly attempt to act against this apostolic protection, let him be struck by the sword of our anathema unless he repents. Whoever guards this command shall deserve the abundance of our blessing.

Given on the third day before the Ides of January, through the hands of Wido, primicerius of Toul and chancellor of the holy apostolic see [Col. 0669C], in the second year of Pope Lord Leo IX, indiction III [1049].

### LIV. Saint Leo IX, at the request of Emperor Henry, confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Saint Maximin of Trier. (Year 1051.)

[Dom Calmet, *History of Lorraine*, I, Documents, p. 434.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the church specially dedicated in the suburb of Trier in honor of Saint John the Evangelist and Saint Maximin the Confessor, and also to Abbot Theodoric, his successors, and the monks serving God there: greetings and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0669D]

The sacred order of the apostolate and the pious devotion of the holy Roman see always demand of us that we vigilantly maintain concern for the churches and worthily provide in all things for the needs of God’s servants.

Therefore, for the love of the Lord and at the petition of our most beloved son, namely Henry, the august emperor, we have decided, following the custom of our predecessors, to confirm by the privilege of our apostolic authority, for the use of the monks serving God in the aforesaid monastery, the churches and estates specifically belonging to their provisions.

We therefore wish and decree by the authority of the sacred first see that the churches, estates, and possessions granted or assigned for the prebend of the aforesaid brothers by kings and emperors—namely Dagobert, Pippin, Charles, Louis [Col. 0670A], Arnulf, Henry, Conrad, and the brothers Otto, as well as by our aforesaid most beloved son, Henry the most august emperor—shall suffer violence from no person, great or small. Rather, from them the monks shall receive food and clothing.

These are: Apula, Schwabenheim, Brincisheim, Evernisheim, Heinfinesheim, Vehinoheim, Scheringesfell, Budenheim, Alsontia, Basinbach, Siemera, Mamendal, Narheim, and Luesderovorf; and from these churches, Gozolvesheim, Albucha, Weldenotein, Wanheim, Flanheim, and Nusum; and from the estate of Gundershausen and the places belonging to it, namely Buosbach, Holtzhausen, Daffendal, and Sueppenhausun.

Also, from these places: Rivenacha, Leovum, Gracho, the tithe of the valley with its dependencies, Mayrchidilh, Billiche, Keriskee [Col. 0670B], Daleheim, Bislee, Wilre, Druhdildinga, Mambra, Murm, Iringa, the church at Steinsela, Diedenhovum, Wimares, Kircha, Berge, Crusta, Luterens, Darre, Tavena, Lindiche, Mersche, Bisanga, and whatever they possess within and outside the city of Metz, in houses, vineyards, fields, or small plots; and whatever they possess in the district of Bingen, in these places: Ratheresdorf, Bustal, Franchingun, Ebeno, and Meisbrach; or whatever belongs to the same monastery beside the River Mass in Carmiringun and Fractura, or in the district of Eifel, in these places: Vahisheim and Lieznich.

Also, a certain estate called Prichina, situated in the district of Einrich, which our aforesaid most beloved son, Henry the august emperor, had taken away from the same brothers some years earlier, he restored, after being admonished by the protection of our apostolic authority [Col. 0670C]. He confirmed by his command that no one should thereafter withdraw it from the brothers’ prebend or assign it to anyone else, and he most devoutly requested that we do the same.

Thus the brothers shall sometimes receive lard from the aforesaid estate and the places belonging to it; according to the command of the holy rule they shall receive guests; and, caring for the sick and weak, they shall faithfully provide from those resources for the use of pilgrims and the poor. They shall also receive from them breeches, mantles, and tablecloths for necessary use.

Therefore, so that the same brothers may hold under their care the aforesaid places with all their dependencies, and all the churches of the entire abbey, together with the tithes, endowment, and dotal properties belonging to them [Col. 0670D], as well as all the Salic tithes which we grant for the use of guests, pilgrims, and the poor, and so that they may securely, quietly, and peacefully possess them according to their own judgment, we strengthen these provisions for them by divine invocation and by this apostolic confirmation of ours.

No emperor, king, abbot, duke, count, viscount, or person of ecclesiastical dignity or worldly condition, great or small, shall presume to grant anything from them to any free man, to a servant of another church or lord, or to any minister, or to alienate it in any way from the brothers’ prebend. Rather, since it ought to be subject to the law of the holy apostolic see and is known to stand under the protection of kings and emperors, it shall remain perpetually, without any opposition, for the use of the monks [Col. 0671A].

But if anyone—which God forbid—should presume with wicked boldness to violate or in any way infringe what we or other most holy pontiffs, our predecessors in the Holy Roman Church, have established for the praise of almighty God and the stability of the aforementioned venerable monastery, we bind him irrevocably by the bond of anathema, by the authority of almighty God, through the intercession of blessed Peter, chief of the apostles, whose office we exercise, and by the apostolic constitution of our humility.

Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February, through the hands of Udo, chancellor and librarian of the holy apostolic see and primicerius of Toul, in the second year of Pope Lord Leo IX, indiction IV, in the year 1051 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

### LV. Saint Leo IX confirms the goods of the canons of the principal and major church of Lucca. (Year 1051.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, I, 805.]

[Col. 0671B]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the canons of the principal and major church in the city of Lucca, serving God and Saint Martin the Confessor there by leading a regular life and preserving chastity: everlasting salvation in the Lord.

Since great care must be applied to securing the goods of the churches, so that the souls and bodies of those who desire to serve the holy altar chastely and according to rule may be preserved, this must be pursued with all the more eager concern. While they labor faithfully in serving there, they ought to receive food and clothing for canonical use [Col. 0671C], lest, while seeking these things out of necessity, they incur the fault of wandering.

Therefore, wishing to provide a benevolent settlement and a kindly provision for this deficiency of yours, by this page of apostolic authority we desire that everything which you now possess for the common use of regular life, or shall possess perpetually, whether by the grant of your bishop—who is now your benevolent and cheerful helper, our brother and fellow bishop John—or by that of his successors, or through the charitable donation of any faithful persons, shall be valid and confirmed for you and in no way violable.

And if the Lord God, mercifully regarding the humility of his Church, should free your church from married priests, who are altogether to be excluded from the Lord’s offering [Col. 0671D], let the chaste be restored in place of the incestuous and the clean in place of the impure; and let the ecclesiastical goods which those men dissipate by living luxuriously be brought into the common use of those canonically dwelling together. Thus may their more desirable death become the most desired salvation of the pastoral household, and may this faithful community suffer no annoyance from its bishop in the granting of prebends, whether through payment or sale.

Until now, therefore, there was darkness; now, however, there is light in the Lord. Walk as children of light, so that with one mind and one voice you may honor God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever. May he preserve and strengthen you in fraternal concord. May the one who dissipates your congregation be dissipated; may resistance be offered to the one who contradicts.

May any bishop of yours who is ignorant of this be likened to the one of whom it is said, “Every ignorant person shall be ignored.” We desire that your coadjutor, always assisted by Saint Martin, may rejoice in the divine recompense, truly saying: “Our help is in the name of the Lord.”

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of March, through the hands of Frederick, chancellor and vicegerent of Lord Herman, archchancellor of the holy apostolic see and archbishop of Cologne, in the third year of Pope Lord Leo IX, indiction IV.

### LVI. Saint Leo IX confirms certain possessions of the Church of Toul at the request of Bishop Udo. (Year 1051.)

[Defense of the Church of Toul, Documents, p. 12.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Udo, bishop [Col. 0672B] of the holy Church of Toul, and through him to all his successors: greetings and apostolic blessing.

If we render assistance to those serving the needs of holy Mother Church, we confidently hope that this will increase our salvation through the reward of heavenly recompense; and when their holy devotion to divine worship is more fervently increased through us, we trust that we shall receive no small share in the reward of their recompense from the eternal Judge.

Therefore, Udo, dearest son, it seemed right and salutary to us that we should shield with apostolic authority the benefits, both ecclesiastical and secular, belonging to the episcopal table of the Church of Toul and subject to its dignity, and decree that they remain free and inviolable [Col. 0672C] from everyone, whatever their condition or profession.

Accordingly, by that authority through which, though unworthy, we nevertheless exercise on earth the office of the most blessed Apostle, the prince of the apostles, Peter, we confirm and strengthen by this page of our privilege the possessions listed in the following letter, which from ancient times down to our own we have heard of and known to have remained undisturbed and without dispute. These are: the abbey of Saint Aper with all its dependencies; the abbey of Saint Mansuetus with all its appurtenances; and also the abbey of the Median monastery, situated in the county of Colmont in the Vosges, above the Rabason River, dedicated in honor of Saint Peter with all its dependencies. Our predecessor Gauselinus, a venerable bishop, compassionately yielding like a father to its wretched servitude and desolation, obtained it from the grandfather and father of Lord Otto the emperor, with the greatest distinction of character and wisdom, for the enlargement of the Church of Toul and to relieve the poverty of the monks, who had already been driven into exile by the power of secular wickedness. In the same way, Lord Otto the emperor reinvested our predecessor, Saint Gerard, with the whole of it, so that it might be restored, without anyone’s opposition, to be held perpetually under the lordship of the Church of Toul. At the same time, together with the abbeys named above, we establish and confirm the abbey called Buxerias, dedicated in honor of the holy Mother and Virgin of God, and the abbey of Saint Menna the virgin, [Col. 0673A] in the place called Portussuavis, and the abbey of Saints Bertarius and Attalenus, in the place called Bledericivilla.

Likewise, dearest son Udo, we confirm to you and to your Church the abbey of Saint Peter and Saint Bercharius, situated in the Dervo forest, and the abbey of Saint Genulphus of Verone, with its dependencies. We also confirm the estates, with all their dependencies, belonging to the service and episcopal table, namely: a certain estate at Bercheim, which Bishop Gauzelinus received from the aforesaid kings as sufficiently necessary for his own use and that of his successors, held peacefully, and left to succeeding bishops; and also the market of that estate, with its ban and mint, which the glorious Emperor Henry perpetually granted to you, dearest son, and to your Church. We also confirm the abbey of the Holy Savior with all its possessions; the estate of the monastery of Bodo with everything belonging to it; the estate of Berga; the estate of Leberduno; the estate of Luciaco; the estate of Scrupulo; the estate of Brureyo; the estate of Buckileio; the estate of Bonivilla; the estate of Salvineio; the estate of Parneio above the Meuse; the estate of Blamiaco; and the village of Caldeniacum with all its dependencies, its woods, meadows, vineyards, pastures, watercourses, cultivated and uncultivated lands, and serfs. We also confirm the estate of Archiriacum, situated not far from the valley of Saint Deodatus, with everything belonging to it.

Likewise, we confirm to the holy Church of Toul [Col. 0673C] the monastery of Saint Deodatus, formerly an abbey and called Galilee, situated in the Vosges forest, in territory surrounded on every side by that of the Church of Toul, owing in its entirety from the founder himself, by reason of the antiquity of its foundation, to the Church of Toul. Formerly, our predecessors the bishops recovered it from King Otto, at the appeal of our predecessor Saint Gerard, and held it in its entirety, possessing in this matter both a royal charter and an apostolic privilege of the Roman see. It had been taken away from the place of Toul by fraudulent usurpation and granted as a benefice to laymen through injury and hatred, and especially through the zeal, anger, and envy of the excommunicated King Lothair.

We confirm that the County of Toul belongs wholly to the authority of the see of Toul. The aforementioned Bishop Gauzelinus obtained it in its entirety from the grandfather and father of Lord Otto the emperor. Let no holder of an ecclesiastical benefice transfer the Church’s benefices into allodial ownership, since this would be contrary to the law of God and sacrilegious. We, who were brother and bishop of the holy Church of Toul, saw all these aforesaid possessions, held them in lawful and undisturbed possession, and kept them in peace. We also confirm those not named here, whether already acquired or still to be acquired, which the Church of Toul may lawfully retain by legitimate title or donation.

Therefore, under solemn appeal to the just judgment of God, we establish and confirm that no person, whatever his rank, profession, or sex, shall presume to act against this privilege and confirmation of our apostolic authority. Whoever dares to presume such an act shall, by divine vengeance, by the authority of the apostles Peter and Paul, and by our apostolic anathema, remain struck outside the Church of Christ’s faithful until he has offered worthy satisfaction. But whoever safeguards it shall be sanctified by our blessing and made a participant in eternal life. Amen.

In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1051.

Given at Rome on the eighth day before the Kalends of April.

### LVII. Saint Leo IX releases Edward, king of the English, from his vow to go to Rome because of the seditious condition of his kingdom, and orders him to distribute among the poor the money allocated for the journey and to spend it on founding a new monastery of Saint Peter or repairing an old one. (Year 1051.)

[Labbe, *Councils*, XI, 1189.]

[Col. 0674B]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Edward, king of the English, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since we have recognized your praiseworthy will, pleasing to God, we give thanks to God, through whom kings reign and rulers decree what is just. But because the Lord is near in every place to those who call upon him in truth, and because the holy apostles, joined to their head, are one spirit and hear pious prayers equally; and because it is clear that the English region is endangered by your departure—you who restrain its seditious movements with the bridle of justice—we, by the authority of God, the holy apostles, and the holy synod, absolve you from the sin of that vow, for which you fear offending God, and from all your negligences and iniquities, exercising that power which the Lord granted us in blessed Peter, saying: “Whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven” (Matthew 16).

Furthermore, under the name of holy obedience and penance, we command you to distribute among the poor the expenses you had prepared for that journey, and either to build a new monastic community in honor of Saint Peter, prince of the apostles, or to repair and enlarge an old one, and to provide the brothers with sufficient food from your revenues. Thus, while they continually praise God there, glory may be increased for the saints and indulgence granted to you. Whatever you have given, or whatever has been given or shall be given to that place, we command by apostolic authority to remain valid. We also decree that it shall always be a dwelling of monks and shall be subject to no lay person except the king. Whatever privileges you may wish to establish there that pertain to the honor of God, we grant and confirm with the strongest authority, and we condemn those who violate them with eternal curse.

### LVIII. Saint Leo IX confirms the possessions of the Church of the Holy Trinity of Pescara. (Year 1051.)

[Muratori, *Italian Historical Writers*, II, ii, 860.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Dominicus, venerable abbot of the Church of the holy and undivided Trinity, which is on the island of Pescara, also called Casa Aurea, where the body of blessed Clement, pope and [Col. 0675A] martyr, rests, and to your successors forever.

It is fitting that our apostolic office should come to the aid of those who make worthy requests with benevolent compassion and should grant support to the minds of those who ask with eager devotion. For from this we shall unquestionably obtain the richest reward from God, the Creator of all, when, assenting to pious petitions, we restore and set right through our pious governance those things that have been distorted or unjustly taken away.

Therefore, dearest brother, since we know that you seek rather to enlarge the goods of your Church as far as your ability permits than to diminish or destroy them, we open to your upright petition, with the charitable affection that is fitting, the door of apostolic mercy. Through the sacred [Col. 0675B] privilege of our supreme see, we confirm and strengthen that your Church shall possess, without any injury or disturbance, everything it has possessed until now, possesses now, or shall possess in the future.

Accordingly, by the apostolic authority of Peter, prince of the apostles, and by our own authority, which we exercise in his place, we command and prohibit that no one living under the jurisdiction of our apostolic rule—whether emperor, king, duke, marquis, archbishop, bishop, count, viscount, or any collector of anything, whether lay or ecclesiastical, or any person of whatever condition, great or small—presume to invade, sell, violate, or disturb the aforesaid goods of the Church, whether in cells and castles, villages and estates, or possessions, and whatever lawful regalia it possesses anywhere in districts or territories by written charters or royal grants.

But if anyone should [lacuna] presume, or consent to those who presume to do so, or become their supporter, and should not instead strive to observe it in its entirety, but presume to transgress this apostolic command and prohibition, let him know that by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles and key-bearer of the kingdom of heaven, and by the bond of our anathema, he is bound and alienated from the kingdom of God, and is designated, according to the canonical tradition of the holy Fathers, as a transgressor, together with the devil and his most dreadful pageantry. For it is written that no one may presume to transgress the boundaries of our fathers through any unlawful act of presumption; and because necessity requires that, for your sake, transgressors be restrained by the bridle of canonical correction. Moreover, may he lose his soul by the spiritual dart of the one whose ear Malchus lost by the temporal sword. But whoever proves himself an observer shall be enriched by the gift of apostolic blessing. Farewell.

Given on the tenth day before the Kalends of July, through the hand of Frederick, deacon, librarian, and chancellor of the holy apostolic see, acting in place of Lord Herimann, archbishop of Cologne and archchancellor, in the third year of Lord Pope Leo IX, indiction 4.

### LIX. Saint Leo IX confirms the metropolitan rights of the Church of Salerno, at the request of Archbishop John. (Year 1051.)

[Baronius, under the year 1051, vol. XI, 195.]

[Col. 0676A]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the holy and venerable Church of Salerno, which belongs to blessed Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, where also the glorious body of Matthew the apostle and evangelist rests with blessed Fortunatus the martyr, and through it to our fellow-brother John, archbishop of that same Church, forever.

To assume priestly office, if we consider it with inward vigilance, is more a burden than an honor; for one cannot adequately care for one’s own affairs unless one has also wisely managed those of others. The reason he undertakes the care of pastoral government is that he may receive upon himself, with pious foresight, responsibility for others and arrange himself vigilantly for their protection, lest, God forbid, through our negligence the envious enemy should devour anyone in his ravenous throat, and the destruction of those entrusted to us should justly be charged to our punishment because we neglected to guard them with watchful care.

Let us therefore perform what we say, and let us hasten to benefit as much as we can those whom, by the dispensation of divine counsel, we have been appointed to govern, so that when the creditor comes to settle accounts with us, he may find that we have made a profit and may gladden us with his promised reward. Since at present we cannot honor, enrich, or enlarge this Church with any goods of our own, as is fitting, we judge it pious to confirm its own possessions for it and preserve them undivided and undiminished.

Therefore, gladly assenting to the petition of our brother Archbishop John, we have decreed that this privilege of our apostolate be made, establishing by apostolic judgment that whatever emperors, kings, princes, or the man who now rules with distinction, Guatmarius, have granted to this house of the Lord, and everything granted by any of Christ’s faithful or to be granted in perpetuity, shall always remain valid and inviolate.

We also confirm to you the archbishopric of Salerno in its entirety, with its adjacent parishes. Furthermore, we grant you the license and authority to ordain and consecrate in the places subject to us, namely: the bishopric of Paestum with its parishes [Col. 0676D] and dependencies; Nola; and Conza with their parishes and dependencies; as well as Malvito and Cosenza; and likewise the bishopric of Bisignano and the bishopric of Acerenza with all their parishes and dependencies. You shall also be permitted to ordain bishops over suitable places, according to the rule of the holy Fathers, within the full integrity of the archbishopric of Salerno. Nor shall our successors henceforth ever have authority to consecrate bishops in all the aforesaid bishoprics which we have granted to you by apostolic authority, just as this has been granted to you.

But if anyone should presume to act against this privilege of our command, or consent to those who presume to do so, or become their supporter, and should not instead strive to observe it intact, but presume to transgress this apostolic command and prohibition, let him know that by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles and key-bearer of the kingdom of heaven, and by the bond of our anathema, he is bound and alienated from the kingdom of God, and is designated, together with the devil and his most dreadful pageantry, as a transgressor according to the canonical tradition of the holy Fathers. For it is written: “No one may presume to transgress the boundaries of our fathers through any unlawful act of presumption” (Proverbs 22). And since necessity requires, for your sake, that transgressors be restrained by the bridle of canonical correction, may he moreover lose his soul by the spiritual dart of the one whose ear Malchus lost by the temporal sword. [Col. 0677B] But whoever observes the constitution and confirmation of this privilege of ours, may he be blessed by the Lord God and, through the intercession of Matthew the evangelist, deserve to become a participant in the eternal kingdom.

Given on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August, through the hand of Frederick, deacon, librarian and chancellor of the holy apostolic see, and of Lord Herimann, archbishop of Cologne and archchancellor, in the third year of Lord Pope Leo IX, indiction 4.

### LX. Saint Leo IX confirms and enlarges the privileges of the monastery of Saint Mary situated on the island of Gorgona. (Year 1051.)

[Ughelli, *Sacred Italy*, III, 358.]

Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the Church of holy Mary, Mother and Virgin of God, on the island of Gorgona, where the body of blessed Gorgonius also rests, and through it to you, Bono, abbot, and to your successors forever.

It is fitting for apostolic governance to fulfill the desire of those who make right requests and to grant support to just supplications.
