Therefore, whoever does not remain with us but goes out from us is plainly an Antichrist. And how are they proved to be Antichrists? By a lie. ‘And who is a liar except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ?’ (ibid., 22).

> “Let your Charity observe this great mystery. Attend to what the Lord God has inspired and what I wish to suggest to you. Look: they went out from us and became Donatists. Let us ask them whether Jesus is the Christ. At once they confess that Jesus is the Christ. If, then, the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ is an Antichrist, they cannot call us Antichrists, nor can we call them Antichrists, since both we and they confess him. If, then, neither they call us Antichrists nor we call them Antichrists, neither they went out from us nor we from them.

> “If they did not go out from us, we are in unity. If we are in unity, what are two altars doing in this city? What are divided households and divided marriages doing? What is a common bed and a divided Christ doing? The truth admonishes us to confess what is true: either they went out from us or we from them. But far be it from us that we should have gone out from them! We possess the testament of the Lord’s inheritance. Let us read it and find ourselves there:

> “‘I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and your possession to the ends of the earth’ (Ps. II, 8).

> “We hold Christ’s inheritance, but they do not hold it. They do not share with the whole world; they do not share with the universal Church redeemed by the blood of the Lord” [Col. 1105B].

And shortly afterward:

> “If, then, they went out from us, they are Antichrists. If they are Antichrists, they are liars. If they are liars, they deny Jesus Christ. The difficulty of the question returns. Ask each one individually: they confess that Jesus is the Christ. This Epistle’s narrow meaning constrains us. You see the question. This question troubles both us and them if it is not understood. Either we are Antichrists or they are Antichrists.

> “But this Epistle has identified the Antichrists. Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ is himself an Antichrist. Let us therefore seek who denies him, and let us not attend to the tongue but to deeds. For if everyone is questioned, everyone confesses with one mouth that Jesus is the Christ. Let the tongue be silent for a little while; question the life.

> “If we find this, if Scripture itself tells us that denial is made not only with the tongue but also by deeds, then certainly we find many Antichrists who profess Christ with their mouths but disagree with Christ in their conduct. Where do we find this? In Scripture. Ask Paul and listen. Speaking about such people, he says: ‘They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny him’ (Titus I, 16).

> “We find these people to be Antichrists. Whoever denies Christ by deeds is an Antichrist. I do not listen to what sounds forth; I see what benefits. Deeds speak, and yet we seek words. ‘Hypocrites, how can you speak good things when you are evil?’ (Matt. XII, 34).

> “You bring your voices to my ears; I examine your thoughts. There I see an evil will, while you display false fruits. Do you know what I gather from there? I do not gather figs from thistles; I do not gather grapes from thorns. Every tree is known by its fruits.

> “The Antichrist who professes with his mouth that Jesus is the Christ but denies him by his deeds is the greater liar. He is a liar because he says one thing and does another.”

From these words of so great a teacher, let the Simonians not insolently press us, nor presume to dwell with us in Catholic unity on the grounds that there is one altar for them and for us, and one marriage, and that they are not shown to differ from us in any aspect of their conduct. Let them know that this is attributable to our ignorance or negligence, and to their own fraud and shamelessness. Although they are truly Antichrists, they pretend to be of Christ; and the more dangerous they are, the more perniciously they press upon Christ’s sheepfold under the pretext of fellowship, pretending to be suckling sheep while, under the sacraments of the Catholic Church as though under the coverings of sheep, they continually lie in wait for Catholics and, through their lamb-like jaws, carry out bloody slaughter.

Like their author Judas, under the sign of peace or a kiss, and under the symbol of one communion, they devise and carry out betrayals and massacres from within the Church in numbers all the greater the more secretly their wickedness is preserved. For, like assassins, they pretend to be companions on the journey; then suddenly drawing the dagger from concealment, they attack the unsuspecting, who suspect nothing of the kind, amid friendly conversation—taught to wage war through peace. They are the equals of the impious Manichaeans, who, lest they be detected, even dared with sacrilegious mouths to claim communion with Catholics. Yet they were sometimes detected by this: abstaining from the wine of Christ’s blood, which they did not believe had been poured out for the remission of sins, they withdrew from it. [Col. 1106B]

So, too, we cannot detect these men except when we discover them attempting to sell the grace of the Holy Spirit. But however much they conceal and disguise themselves, they are nevertheless, together with the Manichaeans and other heretics, cast out from the Church as truly heretics; and, as the first of all to be anathematized and cut off, whether they falsely appear to be within or truly are outside, they are Antichrists.

Nor are they like certain Catholics who are still opposed to Christ in Christian living, although they agree with Christ in Christian belief. These men are Antichrists in both respects, because they are opposed to him both through perverse belief and through wicked practice—which, even if it appears good, is nothing but sin, because it is without faith. Against their evasions we are marked by this distinctive saying: “You received without payment; give without payment” (Matt. 10:8).

## CHAPTER XXVIII. Also by the same author as above: that heretics do not have the Holy Spirit, although they possess visible sacraments

But let us still attend to certain sayings of that same teacher:

“Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God” (1 John 4:1).

And who is it who tests the spirits? He has proposed a difficult matter to us, my brothers. It is good for us that he himself should say from what we may distinguish them. He is going to say, “Do not be afraid”; but first look, pay attention. See that this expresses the very point concerning which foolish heretics bring accusations against us. Pay attention and see what he says: “Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God.”

The Holy Spirit is called by the name of water in the Gospel, when the Lord cried out and said: “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, rivers of living water will flow from his belly” (John 7:38). What is that water? Let no one ask me; ask the Gospel: “He said this,” it says, “about the Spirit whom those who believed in him were going to receive” (ibid., 39).

The water of the sacrament, therefore, is one thing, and the water of the Spirit another. The water of the sacrament is visible; the water of the Spirit is invisible. The former washes the body and signifies what takes place in the soul. Through that Spirit the soul itself is cleansed and nourished. It is that Spirit of God which heretics, and all who cut themselves off from the Church, cannot possess,” and so forth.

Here the Catholic judgment of a Catholic teacher is clearly shown: only visible sacraments, without any invisible sanctification—which is undoubtedly the Holy Spirit—remain among heretics. Thus only the visible bread of the sacrament is present to them, while the invisible bread of the Spirit is absent. The same must likewise be believed concerning the water of baptism, the anointing of sanctification, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments.

Would that the visible sacraments themselves had remained pure to them, as they appear to be, and simple, existing only in their own nature, without any pollution within them. But what is worse, it is the bread of pollution and deceit; and whatever belongs to them is as the Holy Spirit testifies through the prophet Hosea, under the name of Ephraim, saying:

“Ephraim has returned to Egypt, and in Assyria he has eaten what is polluted. They shall not pour out wine to the Lord, and their sacrifices shall not please him, like the bread of mourners. All who eat it shall be defiled, because their bread shall not enter into the house of the Lord” (Hos. 9:3–4). “Altars have become for him occasions of sin; they shall offer sacrifices, they shall slaughter flesh and eat it, but the Lord will not accept them” (Hos. 8:11, 13).

Concerning their teachers he had already said:

“They sow the wind and shall reap the whirlwind. The standing stalk has no ear; it shall produce no flour. And if it should produce any, strangers shall eat it” (Hos. 8:7). “The prophet is a snare of ruin upon all his ways; madness is in the house of his God. They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gibeah” (Hos. 9:8–9). [Col. 1107C]

If it is asked what the sin of Gibeah was, the Book of Judges clearly shows it: it relates that some of the inhabitants of Gibeah were effeminate men, others Sodomites, and others their defenders. Such, without doubt, are the gatherings of heretics, who make the house of God a den of thieves and a brothel.

Let their hearers not rejoice, as Catholics do, in the Spirit of God: “Do not rejoice like the peoples, for you have fornicated away from your God” (Hos. 9:1). And specifically noting the Simoniac heresy, he adds: “You have loved payment above all the threshing floors of grain” (ibid.).

A little later:

“Ephraim has surrounded me with denial, and the house of Israel with deceit” (Hos. 11:12).

“Canaan, with a deceitful balance in his hand, has loved oppression. And Ephraim said: ‘Nevertheless I have become rich; I have found an idol for myself. None of my labors will find in me the iniquity that I have committed’” (Hos. 12:7–8). [Col. 1107D]

That none of the sacraments which are thought to be present among heretics benefit their hearers, he shows by saying:

“The threshing floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the wine shall disappoint them. They shall not dwell in the land of the Lord” (Hos. 9:2–3).

“You have plowed iniquity and reaped impiety; you have eaten the fruit of deceit” (Hos. 10:13).

He also predicts that both the people and their leader are to be cast out from the Church:

“From my house I shall cast them out; I shall not continue to love them. All their princes are deserters; their root is dried up; they shall produce no fruit. And even if they should bear children, I shall kill the dearly beloved offspring of their womb. My God shall reject them, because they have not listened to him, and they shall be wanderers among the nations” (Hos. 9:15, 17).

Moreover, since Ephraim, who is also Israel separated from Judah, represented the type of heretics, while Judah represented Catholics, let us now learn how God weighs the works of both:

“Judah descended as a witness with the Lord, and remained faithful with the holy ones” (Hos. 11:12).

“Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the scorching wind. All day long he multiplies lies and desolation; he made a covenant with the Assyrians and carried oil into Egypt” (Hos. 12:1)—that is, he carried his sanctification, or his mercy toward the poor, from inner things into outer darkness.

“Therefore the Lord has a judgment against Judah” (ibid.), namely, discernment and truth.

And because heretics both invoke the Lord and do not invoke him, it is said:

“They called to me: ‘My God, we, Israel, know you’” (Hos. 8:2),

“but they did not cry to me from their heart; they howled upon their beds. They ruminated over grain and wine” (Hos. 7:14). [Col. 1108B]

Howling, therefore, belongs to wolves. Hence it is evident that heretics do not pray to God but howl. This applies above all to the Simonians, who, like ravenous and hungry wolves, raise no voices to God except to fill the belly of their wickedness through profit. Over the grain and wine of the offering they do not pray but ruminate, because they recall nothing there except their customary food—that is, money.

Thus the Simoniac thief, entering the house of the Lord, plunders the little thieves outside, depriving even his lesser dependents of the visible sacraments through his own childish understanding when he sells them.

## CHAPTER XXIX. Also by the same author as above, and concerning the same subject: how the Spirit of God is recognized

Now let the response to the question previously posed be drawn from blessed Augustine, and let it touch briefly upon what that teacher, characteristically expansive, pours forth to the people in orderly and detailed explanation. (Augustine, *Tractate 6 on the Epistle of John*, no. 11.)

“If the Holy Spirit is signified under the name of water, and this Epistle says, ‘Do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God’ (1 John 4:1), let us understand that this is what is meant: ‘Keep away from alien water, and do not drink from an alien fountain’ (Prov. 5:15). What does ‘You shall not drink from an alien fountain’ mean? You shall not believe an alien spirit.

“There remains, therefore, an examination by which it may be proved which spirit is the Spirit of God. He did indeed provide a sign, and perhaps this is difficult. Nevertheless, let us see. We shall return to that charity. It is charity that teaches us, because it is itself the anointing.

“Yet what does he say here? ‘Test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into this world’ (1 John 4:1). All heretics and all schismatics are already there. How, then, shall I test the Spirit? It follows: ‘By this the Spirit of God is known: every spirit that does not confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh is not from God, and this is the spirit of Antichrist, of which you have heard that it is to come, and it is now in this world’ (ibid., 2–3).

“Then the spirit which is among heretics is from God, because they confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh? At this point they perhaps raise themselves up against us and say: ‘You do not have the Spirit from God, but we too confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh.’

“Yet he denied that they possess the Spirit of God, because they do not confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh. Ask the Arians: do they confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh? Ask the Macedonians: do they confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh? Ask the Cataphrygians: do they confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh? Ask the Novatians: do they confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh? Do all these heresies therefore possess the Spirit of God? Then they are not false prophets? Then there is no deception or seduction among them?

“Certainly they are Antichrists, who went out from us, but they were not of us. What, then, shall we do? From what shall we distinguish them? Let us attend to their works, not to the noise of their tongue. Let us ask why Christ came in the flesh, and we shall discover who denies that he came in the flesh.

“For if you attend to their tongues, you will hear many heresies confessing that Christ came in the flesh; but the truth refutes them. Why did Christ come in the flesh? Because it was necessary that the hope of resurrection be brought to us. God therefore came in the flesh in order to die for us. But how did he die for us? ‘No one has greater love than this: that someone should lay down his life for his friends’ (John 15:13). Love, therefore, brought him to the flesh. Whoever does not have love denies that Christ came in the flesh.

“Now I ask all the heretics: Did Christ come in the flesh? ‘He came; I believe this; I confess this.’ No—you deny this. ‘How do I deny it? Do you hear me saying this?’ Rather, I prove that you deny it, because you deny it. You say it with your voice, but deny it in your heart; you say it in words, but deny it in deeds.

“‘How,’ you ask, ‘do I deny it in deeds?’ Because Christ came in the flesh in order to die for us. He died for us because he taught great love. You do not have love, because for the sake of your own love you divide unity. Understand, therefore, from this where the Spirit is from God.

“Strike, touch the earthen vessels, lest they have perhaps cracked and give a bad sound. See whether they sound whole; see whether love is there. You withdraw yourself from the unity of the whole world; you divide the Church from unity; you tear apart the body of Christ. He came in the flesh to gather; you cry out for the purpose of scattering.

“Therefore that is the Spirit of God which says that Jesus Christ came in the flesh—says it not with the tongue but in deeds, not by making a sound but by loving. But that is not the Spirit of God which denies that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. It too denies him not with the tongue but with its life, not in words but in deeds.

“It is therefore clear, brothers, by what means we recognize them. Many are within, as though they were within; but no one is outside unless he truly is outside. So that you may know this, because he referred to deeds, he says: ‘Every spirit that dissolves Jesus, who came in the flesh, is not from God’ (1 John 4:3).

“What does ‘dissolves’ mean in deeds? What does he show you, who denies that he said ‘dissolves’? He came to gather; you come to dissolve. Do you wish to distinguish the members of Christ? How do you not deny that Christ came in the flesh when, for your own honor, you tear apart the Church of God which he gathered? You come against Christ; you are an Antichrist. Whether you are within or outside, you are an Antichrist. But when you are within, you lie hidden; when you are outside, you are revealed.

“You dissolve Jesus and deny that God came in the flesh. You are not from God. Therefore he dissolves who does not act. What does he teach us except that we should question deeds and not believe words? All who violate love deny that Jesus came in the flesh. For there would have been no need for Jesus to come in the flesh except because of love.

“How could the Son of God lay down his life for us unless he assumed flesh, in which he could die? Whoever violates love—whatever his tongue may say—by his life denies that Christ came in the flesh; and he is an Antichrist wherever he may be, wherever he may enter.

“‘We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever does not know God does not listen to us. By this the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error are recognized’ (1 John 4:6).

“He has now made us attentive, because the one who knows God listens, while the one who does not know him does not listen; and this is the distinction between the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error. Let us see what he is going to admonish us about, in which we must listen to him:

“‘Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God’ (1 John 4:7).”

Also, on the same subject as above (Augustine, *Tractate 7 on the Epistle of John*, no. 11):

“Those who violate love have made a schism. Just as they hate love itself, so they hate the dove. But the dove refutes them. It proceeds from heaven; the heavens are opened, and it remains upon the head of the Lord. Why is this? So that they may hear: ‘This is the one who baptizes’ (John 1:33).

“Withdraw, plunderers; withdraw, invaders of Christ’s possession. In your possessions, where you wish to rule, you have dared to fasten the titles of the Mighty One. He recognizes his titles and vindicates his possession for himself. He does not erase the titles, but enters and takes possession.

“Thus, when someone comes to the Catholic Church, the baptism is not erased, lest the emperor’s title be erased; but it is recognized whose title it is within the Catholic Church. The possessor enters under his own titles, where the plunderer was entering under titles belonging to another.”

The same author, on the same subject as above:

“Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born from God” (Augustine, *Tractate 10 on the Epistle of John*, no. 1).

“Who is it who does not believe that Jesus is the Christ? The one who does not live as Christ commands. For many say, ‘I believe’; but faith without works does not save. The work of faith is love itself, as the apostle Paul says: ‘And faith which works through love’ (Gal. 5:6).

“Your former works, before you believed, were either nonexistent or, if they appeared good, empty. If they were nonexistent, you were like a man without feet, or unable to walk because his feet were injured. But if they appeared good before you believed, you were indeed running, but by running outside the way you were wandering rather than arriving.

“We must therefore both run and run in the way. Whoever runs outside the way runs in vain—or rather, runs toward toil; the farther he runs outside the way, the more he wanders. What is the way along which we run? Christ, who said, ‘I am the way’ (John 14:6). What is the homeland toward which we run? Christ, who said, ‘I am the truth’ (ibid.). Through him we run, toward him we run, and in him we rest. But so that we might run through him, he extended himself even to us.”

The same author, on the same subject as above:

“What more could the demons believe than to say, ‘We know who you are, the Son of God, the Holy One of God’ (Luke 4:34)? What the demons said, Peter also said. The words were the same, but not the intention.

“And how is it clear that Peter said this with love? Because the Christian’s faith is with love of God, whereas the demon’s is without love. How is it without love? Peter said this in order to embrace Christ; the demons said it so that Christ would depart from them. For before they said, ‘We know who you are, the Son of God; what have we to do with you?’ (Mark 1:24), they had said, ‘Why have you come before the time to destroy us?’ (Luke 4:34).

“It is one thing to confess Christ in order to hold Christ; it is another to confess Christ in order to drive Christ away from you. You see, therefore, that when he says here ‘the one who believes,’ it is a particular kind of faith, not simply a common faith shared with many.

“Let no heretic say to you, ‘We too believe.’ For I proposed the example of the demons precisely so that you would not rejoice at the words of those who believe, but examine the deeds of those who live.

“What does it mean to believe in him? ‘Everyone who loves the one who begets loves the one begotten by him.’ He immediately joined love to faith, because faith without love is empty. The Christian’s faith is with love; the demon’s faith is without love.

“Those who do not believe are worse and slower than the demons. Everyone who loves the Father loves the Son. By this we know that we love the children of God. He said ‘children of God’ of those whom just before he called ‘the Son,’ because the children of God are the body of the only Son of God. Since he is the head and we are the members, there is one Son of God.

“Therefore whoever loves the children of God loves the Son of God. And whoever loves the Son of God loves the Father. No one can love the Father without loving the Son. And whoever loves the Son loves the children of God. Which children of God? The members of the Son of God.

“By loving, he himself also becomes a member; through love he is joined into the structure of Christ’s body, and there will be one Christ loving himself. For when the members love one another, the body loves itself. ‘If one member suffers, all the members suffer together; if one member is glorified, all the members rejoice together.’ And what does he say next? ‘You are the body of Christ and individually members of it’ (1 Cor. 12:26–27).

“‘For whoever does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love God whom he does not see?’” (1 John 4:20).

“Extend love throughout the whole world if you wish to love Christ, because the members of Christ lie throughout the world. Be where you ought to be, so that you may be under the head. If you are not in the body, you are not under the head.

“What does it profit that you believe and blaspheme? You adore him in the head and blaspheme him in the body. He loves his body. If you have cut yourself off from his body, the head has not cut itself off from its own body.

“‘You honor me without cause,’ the head cries to you from above; ‘you honor me without cause.’ It is as though someone wished to kiss your head while trampling your feet. Perhaps, wearing hobnailed shoes, he would crush your feet while wishing to hold your head and kiss it. Would you not cry out amid the words of the one honoring you and say, ‘What are you doing, man? You are trampling me’? You would not say, ‘You are trampling my head,’ because he was honoring the head. Yet the head would cry out more on behalf of the trampled members than on its own behalf, because it was being honored.

“Would not the head itself cry out: ‘I do not want your honor; do not trample me now’? Now say, if you can: ‘Why did I trample you?’ Say this to the head: ‘I wanted to kiss you; I wanted to embrace you.’

“But do you not see, foolish man, that whatever you embrace above reaches through the structure of unity to what you trample? You honor me above; you trample me below. What you trample causes more pain than what you honor causes joy, because the one whom you honor grieves for those whom you trample.

“How does the tongue cry out? ‘It hurts me.’ It does not say, ‘It hurts my foot,’ but ‘It hurts me.’ O tongue, who touched you? Who goaded you? Who pricked you? No one. But I am joined to those who are trampled; how can you want me not to grieve, when I am not separated from them?

“The Head, about to ascend into heaven, saw that many would honor him because he had ascended into heaven; and he saw that their honor would be useless if they trampled his members on earth. And lest anyone go astray and, while adoring the Head in heaven, trample his feet on earth, he commended his members on earth. He said where his members would be; he spoke his final words and departed.

“After those words he did not speak on earth. You no longer find Christ speaking on earth. You find him speaking, but from heaven. And why from heaven itself? Because his members were being trampled on earth.

“For he said to the persecutor Saul: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’ (Acts 9:4). I have ascended into heaven, but I still lie upon the earth; here I sit at the right hand of the Father, while there I still hunger and thirst and am a stranger.

“How, then, did he commend his body on earth as he was about to ascend? He answered his disciples: ‘You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth’ (Acts 1:8).

“Behold where I lie, though I ascend. I ascend because I am the head; my body still lies below. Where does it lie? Throughout the whole earth. Beware of striking it; beware of violating it; beware of trampling it.

“These are Christ’s final words as he goes into heaven. Brothers, consider with Christian feeling: if the final words of a father who is about to die and go into the tomb are sweeter, more welcome, and more weighty to his earthly heirs, what should the final words of Christ be to his heirs—not of one returning to the tomb, but of one ascending into heaven?

“And if the final words of a dying father are guarded more carefully by his children, although his body lies senseless in the grave, what do those hope for who do not guard the final words of the one seated in heaven, who sees from above whether he is despised or not—the one who said, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’ (Acts 9:4)?

“He preserves for judgment whatever he sees his members suffer; and the sword of the heretics’ tongues is more grievous and intolerable to them than the sword of the pagans.”

## CHAPTER XXX. Recapitulation of the foregoing words of Saint Augustine

In these clear sayings of the outstanding teacher, all heretical transgressors of the new commandment—and above all the Simonians—must necessarily return to their hearts. They turn the power of the Holy Spirit which they have received into something intended solely for worldly commerce, not for any testimony to Christ. Yet Christ asserted that this power of the Holy Spirit was to be received by his disciples for this one purpose: that they might be witnesses of his resurrection and love everywhere on earth.

But these most perverse men, turned into a twisted bow, attack and strike the one by whom they have been drawn. They presume to distribute for a price the riches of his grace, which they were commanded to set forth and dispense to all freely, just as they had received them freely.

Thus, ungrateful to Christ, they rise up to fight against him with his own gifts, and inflict the worst and incurable wounds upon his faithful as upon his members, because they cannot reach him, who is the head of his own.

Although they sometimes pretend that they wish to honor him with their lips, everything they do is an insult to him, not reverence, so long as they slaughter his faithful through their treachery like thieves and robbers. [Col. 1113B]

They gather them to themselves as though they were simple sheep seduced by a shepherd’s feigned whistle; and so, now secretly, now by force, they sacrifice them in flocks to the devil, while they consent that what cannot otherwise be received except by being given freely should be purchased from them.

Through this contagion a few diseased sheep infect the entire flock, while certain carnal people, afflicted by the disease of ambitious greed, grow tired of the nourishment of heavenly doctrine and withdraw themselves from the eyes of the shepherds along the byways of vice and hide themselves.

Therefore, when they are found by the thieving Simonians like straying sheep, they quickly, because of the excess of their disease, agree with their will. The Simonians wish to kill; these wish to die. The former seek to destroy; the latter do not wish to live. The former seek to ruin; the latter seek to perish.

Thus both they and these devise and carry out a commercial trade in the Holy Spirit, to their own destruction and the contagion of the whole Church, making it carnal or worldly. Their persecution is more grievous to Christ than that of any pagans, who rage against Christians with public savagery and passing wounds, than that of these men, who through hidden conspiracy, under the lamb of peace, inflict everlasting deaths.

If Christ cannot endure persecution of his members without crying out from heaven to Saul, who did not know him and possessed zeal for God, though not according to knowledge, taking away his sight as he cried out, what do we think will happen to these men? They confess that they know God and are rulers of his Church, yet, inflamed with diabolical zeal, knowingly do not cease to persecute and slaughter countless souls of the faithful.

And if Saul was struck with such force for bodily persecution, by how much, do you suppose, are these men struck for spiritual persecution? Hence Saul rightly lost the sight of his bodily eyes for a time; but these men lose the eyes of their hearts, so that thereafter, having themselves become blind guides of the blind, they may fall with their followers into the pit of eternal destruction.

If they recognized themselves as blind, as the Lord says of those like them, they would have no sin, because they would earnestly seek to produce fruits worthy of repentance. But now, because they say, “We see,” their sin remains.

To them the Lord cries from heaven as often as, through his servants in whom he dwells as though in the heavens, he reproves their presumption through the words of the Holy Scriptures. Since he is not heard now, he will later come forth from his chamber into public view, strong and powerful; and like a warrior he will stir up his zeal, raise his voice and cry out, and strengthen himself against his enemies. Then he will say to them:

“I was silent continually; I kept quiet; I was patient. Like a woman in labor I shall speak. You did these things, and I was silent” (Ps. 49:21).

Because you have gradually and partially scattered and swallowed my flock, I shall scatter and swallow you all at once.

## CHAPTER XXXI. On the wickedness of the Simonians, and that they are worse than robbers and without any faith in God

Against these false witnesses, whom Jesus—now incapable of suffering, yet still enduring such men in the sufferings of his Church as he formerly endured in himself—still addresses the Father, saying through the Psalmist:

“Do not hand me over to the souls of those who persecute me, for unjust witnesses have risen against me, and iniquity has lied to itself” (Ps. 26:12).

It is impious to believe that they retain even the smallest spark of love for God and neighbor. For love of God and neighbor is the proper and distinctive virtue of the pious and holy, whereas the other virtues may be shared by good and evil alike.

How could this love exist in those who despise God so greatly that they even strive to sell him at any price, and who hate their neighbor so greatly that they close their own inward parts completely against him, lest he receive freely what God’s generosity wished and commanded to be given freely through them?

Even if they possessed the substance of this world, and closed their inward parts to a neighbor suffering need, giving him nothing freely from what was their own, how would the love of God—which is only doubled in love of God and neighbor—remain in them? (1 John 3:17.)

But these men not only give nothing of their own; in order to give what they received freely from God to be given freely, they strip their wretched neighbor of every good of body and soul. They are so hardened against love that they do not open their mouths to God or neighbor out of love for either, except when money has been given or agreed upon.

How much worse they are than the worst robbers! Other robbers tear apart the body of their neighbor in such a way that they cannot kill the soul as well; these destroy both soul and body.

It is therefore clear that they possess none of the love of God, whom they do not see, since they know so wickedly how to treat their neighbor, whom they do see. If they loved him even to some extent for God’s sake and in God, they would no longer be heretics, because they would necessarily possess as much right faith—even if minimal—as they possessed true love.

But since they possess neither, they are heretics and Antichrists who deny that Jesus came in the flesh. For why did Jesus come in the flesh except to present to himself, from the diverse qualities of human beings and from all the nations of the Gentiles, through the exceeding love by which he laid down his life for them, a glorious Church without spot or wrinkle or anything of that kind (Eph. 5:27)?

In that one spotless dove, his beloved, sister, and immaculate bride, he would rest; and the immaculate Bridegroom himself would rest and reign in the reigning Church. Thus, with all his own perfected into one in himself, the one God himself would be all in all.

This wondrous and desirable union is what these men envy and attack above all others. They do not fear to sell the Holy Spirit, through whom such a great diversity of members is joined, fitted together, and united under one head, Christ, in an irreproachable and incomprehensible composition.

For he, like the strongest and most fervent bitumen or glue of love, which he pours into the hearts of the saints, cements and joins together the body of Christ, formed and prepared through suitable bonds and joints, and causes it to grow into the increase of God. From people of diverse profession and conduct he makes one body and one spirit, according to the calling by which they were called, in one hope.

When these heretics presume to steal him, like the most effective glue, from God’s structure, what great and miserable ruins do they cause? Among them, or in their ruins, nothing orderly will now be found; everything is confused. No beauty remains in them except the squalor of nettles and thorns—namely, of lust and greed—and the horror of a serpent’s hiding place.

## CHAPTER XXXII. How heretics, fornicating away from God, cause others also to fornicate

Behold how those who fornicate away from God, the profane Simonians, stain and destroy that glorious Church which Christ cleansed with the washing of water in the word so that it might be without spot, and for which, so that it might be made without wrinkle, he stretched out its wrinkles upon the scaffold of the cross.

Alas, fornicators now stain her with impunity, contaminating through the contagion of their impurity her washing and the other forms of the divine sacraments granted her from heaven for the preservation of her beauty, and nullifying them through their commerce.

They also wrinkle them, since by the duplicity of their cunning they disfigure her simple intention, like a shining skin. Rightly, therefore, that Bridegroom, “fairer in appearance than the sons of men” (Ps. 44:3), threatens this most beautiful bride of his—whose beauty he delights in above all others—not to begin wandering among the flocks of her companions (Song 1:6), namely, the heretics who, by feeding the flock of their goats, pretend to be friends of the Bridegroom, while jealously claiming the bride not for the Bridegroom but for themselves, and meditating nothing but adultery.

Thus, according to the exposition of blessed Jerome, the Bridegroom threatens the same bride in the Song of Songs and says:

“Either know yourself, because you are the bride of the King and beautiful, and made beautiful by me—for I have presented to myself a glorious Church without spot or wrinkle—or know that, if you do not know yourself and do not recognize your dignity, you will suffer what follows.

“What is that? If you do not know yourself, O fairest among women, go out in the footsteps of the flocks and feed your young goats in the tents of the shepherds; and you will feed not flocks of sheep, not lambs, but your own young goats” (ibid., 7).

For he sets the sheep on his right and the goats on his left. “In the footsteps,” he says, “of the shepherds you will become last—not among sheep, but among your young goats. Living with them, you will not be able to be with me, that is, with the good Shepherd.”

“I have compared you to my cavalry in Pharaoh’s chariots” (ibid., 8).

“If you wish to understand, O bride, how you ought to know yourself, recognize to whom I have compared you, and then you will see yourself as one who ought not to be disfigured when you have recognized your own beauty.

“What, then, does ‘I have compared you to my cavalry in Pharaoh’s chariots’ mean? I know the Bridegroom as a rider, since the prophet says, ‘His riding is salvation.’

“She has therefore been compared to my cavalry in Pharaoh’s chariots. As far as my cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses—as far as I, the Lord, differ from Pharaoh, whom I plunge into the waves, together with his warriors, riders, horses, and chariots—so much better are you, O bride, O ecclesiastical soul, than all the daughters, that is, than all souls that are not ecclesiastical. Therefore, if you are an ecclesiastical soul, you are better than all souls; if you are not better, you are not ecclesiastical.”

[Col. 1116B] For this reason, alas, I greatly fear that, according to the judgment of so prudent a man, that heavenly Bridegroom of his Bride—namely, our Catholic Church—exasperated, as I have already said, by her shameless wandering through the heretics’ enclosures, may give her a writ of divorce and irrevocably say to her: “Go out and depart after the tracks of the flocks, and pasture your kids beside the shepherds’ tents” (Song 1:7).

For she seems to show that she does not know herself, since she is not ashamed to cling to and dwell with profane shepherds in out-of-the-way places—men known to pasture nothing but kids, and even to trade in them. Hence one must take the greatest care lest, through the constant companionship of the kids’ wantonness and the goats’ insolence, her chastity be endangered, and, with adulterers gradually admitted into the Bridegroom’s bedchamber, she be defiled to the very crown of her head, [Col. 1116C] and no longer pasture lambs.

By consenting and communicating with heretics, she makes the kids who are to be placed on the left; from these leaders meanwhile arise, and their fathers, the insolent goats, will in due course arrive—with many curses—at the portion of the devil, abandoned by God, upon whose head and brow the entire Catholic people will invoke their sins, and in whose hell there is no one who confesses to the Lord (Ps. 6:6). They will therefore receive, together with their kids, the lot of the desert of the curse—those who refused to possess the lot assigned to them, the paradise of blessing. They will become the devil’s clergy and Satan’s synagogue, because they refused to be the clergy of God and of the Church.

When this incomparable evil is not vigilantly avoided, it inflicts such uninterrupted losses upon the Church of God [Col. 1116D] that, like the moon during menstruation or at the new moon, although she is whole, she appears either very small or nonexistent. This happens to her because, even when reproved and admonished, she is not ashamed to show that she does not know herself. Hence, by God’s just judgment, she who does not know herself is so unknown even to her own members that many now doubt whether she exists at all.

### CHAPTER XXXIII. On the diminution of the Church and the multiplication of heretics

With the deadly humours of the Simoniac heresy thus embedded in her, the breast of the Catholic Church is oppressed; her judgment is thus weighed down; by an internal and domestic war she is so confused and battered that that Bride, scarcely half-alive, scarcely still palpitates and, like an enormous ship soon to be sunk, loosens her already creaking planks, or, like a once-populous city attacked and conquered by its own inhabitants, at last labors on and scarcely hopes for the safety of any of her own.

Because she despises small things, she gradually falls (Ecclus. 19:1), to the point that she almost no longer knows where she is or whose she is. God alone, amid so many thousands of the worst sellers and buyers, knows who belong to her; to them he speaks daily, gently and familiarly, in the ear of their heart: “Do not fear, little flock, because it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom. Sell what you possess and give alms. Make purses for yourselves that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys. For where your treasure is, there also will your heart be” [Col. 1117B] (Luke 12:32, 34).

But, O Jesus, good Shepherd, how very small now appears the number of these lambs of yours among the countless gatherings of kids! Your most gentle Jacob has now been so overcome by his rough and shaggy uterine brother that, according to Isaiah, thorns and briars are found throughout the whole land for the feeding of kids, while scarcely any pasture remains for the few lambs.

Truly that day foretold by the same prophet has come upon us:

“And it shall come to pass on that day that the glory of Jacob shall be brought low, and the fatness of his flesh shall grow lean. And it shall be as when one gathers in the harvest what remains, and his arm gathers the ears of grain. And it shall be as when one seeks ears of grain in the valley of Raphaim; and what remains in it shall be like a cluster of grapes, and like the shaking of an olive tree—two or three olives at the top of a branch, or four or five on its highest boughs, says the Lord God of Israel” (Isa. 17:4–6).

Then the same prophet adds how much further the Catholic Church suffers diminution even in her smallness:

“Therefore they will plant the planting of the faithless, and sow a foreign shoot” (ibid. 10).

“Alas, alas, alas, Lord God, spare, spare your people, and do not give your inheritance over to destruction” (Joel 2:17)!

“Be gracious, I beg you; cease. Who will raise up Jacob, since he is small?” (Amos 7:2.)

For we have been diminished more than all the nations; and, moreover, those whom we plant become faithless, and we sow a foreign shoot, because, according to Jeremiah’s lament, the enemy consumes those whom we bring up and nourish (Lam. 2:22). And, oh, if only they alone were consumed! But what is more grievous is that those born from the Church’s womb and nourished by her milk later pass from her to the faithless Simon, armed with their mother’s weapons; they rise up cruelly against her and, at the peril of their mother, kill their former brothers, whom they have deceived.

Why, then, does he tear the Church of Christ apart with such hatred and such persistence—she for whose sake alone he came in the flesh—if he does not deny that Christ came in the flesh? For if blessed Father Augustine asserted that the Arians, Macedonians, Cataphrygians, and Novatians deny that Christ came in the flesh because, while holding perverse opinions about his divinity, they rend his Church through their insolence, then the Simoniacs do so much more. They not only hold perverse opinions about God, but also trade in his Church [Col. 1118A] and, as far as lies within their power, reduce her and everything belonging to her almost to nothing.

Certainly, although the Arians perversely say that the Son and the Holy Spirit are lesser than God the Father and are creatures, they do not therefore judge that either of them may be sold. The Macedonians likewise, although they wickedly say that the Holy Spirit is less than the Father and the Son and is a creature, do not do so. Nor do the Cataphrygians, even though they assert that the Holy Spirit came substantially upon Montanus, the founder of their sect. From this alone it is even clearer that the Simoniacs deny that Christ came in the flesh more than all these others: with their mouths they say that the Holy Spirit is in every respect coequal with the Father and the Son, yet they believe that they can sell him daily by shamelessly selling his visible sacraments.

### CHAPTER XXXIV. How much more harmful the Simoniacs are than all heretics

[Col. 1118B]

How much more excusably would the Arians and Macedonians conduct this business if they believed that the Holy Spirit could be sold, since they proclaimed him to be a creature! For it is more consistent that a creature can be sold than that the Creator and Sanctifier of the world can be sold.

Moreover, the fury of those whom manifest terror armed against the Catholic Church more than pretended love is much more tolerable. Public confession declared that they were to be avoided, whereas the Simoniacs are so much more intolerable than they as they are more flattering and more concealed. By their confession we think them Catholics, and by their gentle or peaceful admonition or greeting we take them for fathers [Col. 1118C] or friends. They deliberately use such behavior to cloak their perversity that they may be thought more flattering than the most flattering, although they never cease to destroy the people of God, who do not perceive such great evils—or rather who smile and applaud them.

The holy Seventh Synod, in an irreproachable and authoritative judgment, defined them to be worse than the worst Arians, as was clearly shown above. By comparison with them, even the Novatians may be considered good. The Novatians, carried away by a sect of remarkable continence and the harshest discipline, teach that bigamists and penitents for their crimes ought not to be received by the Church, while in all other matters they in no way contradict the Catholic faith.

But because by their scandal they scandalize and divide the Church, they too deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh—not with their lips, but by their conduct, as nearly all other heretics do. Therefore, if the Novatians, marked by excessive justice, deny that Christ came in the flesh, can there be the slightest doubt that the Simoniacs deny that Christ came in the flesh? They are filled with an elation more than diabolical: they no longer, like the devil, think themselves equal to God through robbery, but superior to him. They believe that he can be separated from them for a price, and they even openly profess this.

By this madness they not only scandalize the Church of God, but—what is utterly intolerable—so undermine her that they completely wrest from her her pledge, namely, the Holy Spirit, by whom she was sealed on the day of redemption and by whom she is sanctified and brought to life, while they transform themselves into ministers of righteousness.

Who would dare even dream that such men believe in the Holy Spirit, whom they attempt to sell more than a thousand times? Could anyone believe this of some worthless little slave, that, having been sold so often, he would endure going away with an even temper, rather than choose flight or any danger in order to escape such an offensive mastership and such profound mockery?

But, shame upon shame, the Spirit of freedom is believed subject to this disgraceful mockery and injury, intolerable even to the lowest slaves, and to obey at the bidding of those who sell him. Their thorns, when they first sprang up, put forward the softness of grass; but now, having long since grown, they reveal the bramble.

Was not the attempt of the faithless Simon like soft grass when compared with the deed of his followers in our own time? For although he wished to buy the Holy Spirit in order to sell him at a higher price, he nevertheless offered his own money, not another’s, for this purpose, as blessed Peter also showed in his reply to him: “May your money be with you unto perdition” (Acts 8:20).

His closer followers are known to have done this very thing when they attempted to purchase ecclesiastical offices solely from their own resources, or from the wealth or possessions of their fathers or friends—chiefly so that those who had previously been powerful and noble through worldly abundance might also, through ecclesiastical rank, rise above the others as more powerful and more noble.

For no rational soul, whether sound or unsound, desires power more than anything else. A sound soul seeks to attain sound power by clinging to the Lord God and placing its hope in him, after the example of the holy angels who remained steadfast. An unsound soul seeks it by withdrawing from God, trusting in itself, or presuming upon itself, after the example of the rebellious spirits who fell from the beginning. Their prince, as the prophet indicates, said in his heart before he fell:

“I will ascend into heaven; above the stars of heaven I will exalt my throne; I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the north; I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High” (Isa. 14:13–14).

### CHAPTER XXXV. On the birth and growth of the Simoniac heresy

Yet this ambition for acquired ecclesiastical dignity, from the time of the apostles until the age of the Christian rulers, deterred by the severity of persecutions, disappeared. The first to be subjected to the most grievous tortures was the one who appeared to be the first ruler and more powerful than the others.

But as soon as peace was restored to the Christians to such an extent that even the emperors submitted their august heads and all the islands of the earth to the feet of Christ’s priests, that ancient plague returned. Seeing such power and such a glorious kingdom and priesthood—within which the saints were already reigning with Christ—it was astonished. Since it was accustomed to desire domination and preeminence, and could not obtain the truth, of which it has no share, it preferred to seize it for itself by deceit.

Hence what the Catholic Church had obtained by the grace of God, Simoniac ambition sought to obtain by money—not in order to remain subject to and serve God’s grace like an adopted son within the Catholic Church, but to rule and command as a tyrant of presumption.

At first, as we have said, they attempted to achieve this at the price of their own money or that of their associates, so that they might rule even the smallest part of the Church. At times they added their immense possessions to ecclesiastical possessions for this purpose and, under the pretext of such an advantage, carried on the business of their ambition. Thus the unlearned might think that the rule of such men not only did no harm but greatly benefited the Church of God, which they enriched from their private resources in order to obtain authority over it by this means.

But since goodness advances by its own degrees, and wickedness likewise by its own, for so long . . . . . . did this somewhat excusable sort of ecclesiastical commerce cling to the Church as long as some measure of Christianity or moral decency remained among our forebears. But when, as sins prevailed, they fell into complete ignorance of God, they cast aside every appearance of excuse or whatever decency there had been. They no longer took care to conceal their avarice but allowed it to rage openly with arms bared. Having at last gained this worst kind of freedom, it drove those greedy for ecclesiastical dignities to the point that they no longer removed or deducted anything from their purses, or those of their associates, or their resources, but scraped together the entire price paid or promised from the revenues or possessions of the churches over which they were placed.

Hence, everywhere, and especially throughout Italy, the churches of God, monasteries, and other religious places may be seen in various conditions: some destroyed and overturned from their foundations; some dug out; some made dreadful by half-collapsed roofs and walls threatening their own ruin [Col. 1120C]; some deserted by human beings and left only to harmful beasts and unclean birds; some filled with thickets and nettles; and some, although they still appear outwardly to stand with their walls and buildings and to be inhabited, found stripped of all their beauty and interior adornment—in books as well as in the vessels and vestments of ecclesiastical ministry—so that of all that devout antiquity had gathered or prepared for holy places, scarcely any little psalter, earthen vessel, or linen corporal remains.

Some, once famous for many and varied estates, castles, municipalities, households, and funds, now retain not even a small field, a tiny hut, a little township, or a donkey or kid—not even anything else that they had possessed. Indeed, the very courtyards of the sanctuaries and the cemeteries of Christians are plowed and cultivated by a foreign farmer and filled with crops or vines.

### CHAPTER XXXVI. How the Simoniacs sell not only the Church’s possessions but also the rulers themselves, together with their peoples, to the devil

In this way the bones of many holy and religious Christians are indiscriminately removed from their own tombs and left naked and rejected upon the surface of the earth like the bones of irrational animals.

Wretched me! I often remember seeing, within the very walls, the floors of once-noble basilicas being plowed and sown, or animals being kept in them. And although such great disasters are not caused so much by a Vandal, Goth, Hun, Lombard, or Hungarian as by the Simoniac enemy, he sells and gives away to relatives and strangers the movable and immovable possessions—and even the living possessions—of venerable places, so wasting and scattering them that he leaves nothing to himself or to his descendants except tears.

Would that he at least plundered only what he found prepared by his predecessors and had at hand in his own time, and not also what he does not yet possess! For by diabolical contracts he sells or gives to secular men the tithes and offerings of the living and the dead, together with all the revenues that the Church was destined to possess after him until the end of the world. In every way and under every condition he can, he alienates them forever, so that those who in future generations are to serve God and work out their own salvation and that of others find nothing at all left for themselves—not even provision for an hour’s food, clothing, or lodging for the night.

Hence the documents in secular hands; hence records on parchment and instruments, inadequately secured by the signatures of such men, by which the ancient charters and canonical privileges of the churches of God are annulled, and every ecclesiastical possession is assigned and confirmed to the right of laymen until the end of the world. The decrees or privileges of Catholic pontiffs can no longer withstand the writings of these heretics; no canons or synods of the holy Fathers can any longer prevail; no edicts or commands of emperors, nor laws of religious rulers, can any longer resist them.

So completely has the adversary prevailed that against him no shield, breastplate, spear, or sword can now stand. All armor turns into straw before him, because he fears neither defense nor any punishment. He mocks the brandished spear and does not consider the trumpet’s blast worth notice, because he treats as a laughing matter the spiritual threat or sentence which, like the stars, strikes from afar, and the carnal condemnation which strikes at close quarters.

He so makes light of any priest’s anathema that, on account of such men, however lowly he may be, any person may disdain to restore to holy places even a foot’s breadth of all that the heretic has confirmed with his own hand. Thus what was first theft, and what gradually became brigandage, has now advanced to such tyranny that whoever seeks to rule churches or cities does not attain it until he has confirmed by oath and in writing, even to the common people, that he will observe and defend the documents of heretics and sacrilegious men.

This is thought a small demand when required of subordinate powers; it is required even of the highest emperors. They are not permitted to receive the insignia of imperial office until they have sworn not only not to annul those documents but also to defend them.

O liberty and piety of the Roman commonwealth! O liberality and power of imperial majesty! The supreme ruler is compelled to swear that he ought not to observe the laws of the religious rulers who preceded him or his own laws, but rather to annul them. He wants those who oppose rendering to God what is God's to render to him what is Caesar's.

Let him consider, I beg, what kind of empire that is which suddenly makes him a pagan instead of a Christian—or rather worse than a pagan, because he apostatizes from God. With the perverse he becomes perverse, with the sacrilegious sacrilegious, and therefore worthy of death, because he consents to those who do such things.

He ought now to be called one who consents to the perverse—or, more truly, one who commands them to do worse things, granting them by his oath the license to retain with impunity what they had seized, and the audacity to seize whatever remains with impunity. For if, as the philosopher says, one who does not prevent sinning when he can is commanding it, how much more is that man commanding it who not only fails to prevent it when he has the power, but even swears that he will never prevent it—while at the same time swearing to God, the holy apostles, and their priests that he will prevent such things and defend ecclesiastical property?

Let whoever can examine how, and by what means, this man escapes the labyrinth: swearing that he will prevent such things, and swearing that he will not prevent them; the one swearing that he will defend the churches’ possessions, the other swearing that he will not defend them.

### CHAPTER XXXVII. On the immeasurable wickedness of the heresy and the beast to which it is compared in the Apocalypse

Thus the wickedness of the people and their own sloth blind the supreme rulers. They neglect to see how terrible the works of God are in his counsels concerning the sons of men (Ps. 65:5), and therefore fall with those whom they ought to govern and beneath those over whom they ought to preside, into the pit of eternal death.

The rulers of the pagans are freer and superior to them even amid the torments themselves, insofar as they were more generous and more ready to preserve and restore to each person his right in worldly affairs. For those rulers, with devout generosity, bestowed privileges upon the pontiffs and temples of their own religion, as they believed it to be, and defended them in their own time with powerful hands. By their laws they also provided future safeguards against every danger of diminution or alienation.

The great Constantine turned their zeal from superstition toward religion, granting to the churches of Christ the privileges that they had granted to their priests and shrines; and his successors—all who were orthodox—have endeavored to do the same down to these dangerous times.

And, oh, how much more tolerable to the churches of Christ are the Arian, Eunomian, Eutychian, or any other heresies! For although in their fury they tear away and scatter God’s sheep like a wolf [Col. 1122D], they do not take away their folds and pastures; they leave them behind so that the remaining and future sheep may dwell there and have food.

For the Catholics receive some consolation for past or present loss when little or certainly nothing has been taken from their food and clothing. Thus, after Auxentius the Arian, Ambrose the Catholic found the support and lodging of the church of Milan left to him; after Maximus the Cynic, Nectarius found the same; and after Dioscorus, Proterius.

If you review the remaining beasts of the heresies, you will find none more harmful than this one, which so plunders Christ’s sheep that afterward no fold or pasture remains for those destined to live after it.

Indeed, this beast not only eats and crushes everything with iron teeth and large ones, and tramples what remains beneath its feet, like that beast which prefigured the Roman Empire; it also emits a flame from itself and leaves nothing before it unconsumed. Therefore, if the prophet, struck with amazement at its power and monstrousness, kept silent about its name, although he did not omit the names of other, terrifying beasts, to what beast will this one be compared? By what name will it be called, since it is found unlike and more cruel than all the others?

Nevertheless, although Daniel—that is, “the judgment of my God”—did not display either the name or the form of the beast that appeared in the prophecy of the fourth kingdom, except for its teeth and feet, the grace of the Lord—that is, John—depicted in his Apocalypse this beast, which represents the prophecy of heresy, suppressing its name alone, as though he had made its visible likeness known to all. He says:

“And I saw another beast rising from the earth. It had two horns like a Lamb and spoke like a dragon. And it exercised all the authority of the first beast”—namely, the beast that was like a leopard, whose feet were like those of a bear and whose mouth was like a lion’s—“in its presence. And it made the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast. And it performed great signs, so that it even made fire come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men. And it deceived those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that were given it to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image of the beast. And it was given power to give breath to the image of the beast, and to cause anyone who would not worship the image of the beast to be killed. And it will make all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slaves, receive a mark on their right hand or on their foreheads, so that no one may buy or sell unless he has the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of its name, and so forth” (Rev. 13:11–18).

Concerning this beast, shortly afterward the angel says to men with a loud voice:

“If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand, he too will drink of the wine of God’s wrath, mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of his anger; and he will be tormented with fire and sulphur in the presence of his holy angels and before the presence of the Lamb. And the smoke of their torments rises forever and ever, and they have no rest day or night, those who worship the beast and its image, and anyone who receives the mark of its name” (Rev. 14:9–11).

[Col. 1123D] Later he calls that second beast the false prophet, saying:

“And I saw from the mouth of the dragon, and from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs. For they are spirits of demons performing signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole earth to gather them for battle on the great day of God Almighty. Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who watches and keeps his garments, so that he may not walk naked and they may not see his shame” (Rev. 16:13–15).

And shortly afterward:

“And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered to make war against him who sat upon the horse and against his army. And the beast was seized, and with it the false prophet who performed signs before it, by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of burning fire and sulphur. The rest were killed by the sword of him who sat upon the horse, the sword that comes from his mouth; and all the birds were filled with their flesh” (Rev. 19:19–21).

After this, concerning the glory of the saints even in the present age, he says:

“And I saw thrones, and those seated upon them, and judgment was given to them. And I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of the testimony of Jesus and because of the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, nor received its mark on their foreheads or on their hands. They lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years. But the rest of the dead did not live until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is the one who has a share in the first resurrection. Over these the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him for a thousand years” (Rev. 20:4–6).

### CHAPTER XXXVIII. Recapitulation of the preceding judgment from the Apocalypse

Since this apostolic prophecy is expounded by the holy Fathers in many ways and at great length, we think it sufficient to indicate briefly from it that the first beast, like a leopard, whose feet were those of a bear and whose mouth was that of a lion, specifically represented the Antichrist. His dominion would arise with marvelous speed and extremely crafty rapacity, and his temporal life would end with extraordinary rapidity, namely after forty-two months.

For the leopard is a variegated, bloodthirsty, swift, rapacious, and headlong animal, so much so that it rushes to its death in a leap, because, as Jeremiah says, it cannot change its spots (Jer. 13:23). Its feet are the feet of a bear: namely, all heretics who, pretending to possess a certain form of human sagacity as though it were divine reason, are more harmful the lower they are in the body of the Antichrist.

By them the structure of all its members is held together and governed; by them the whole mass of the devil’s body is sustained, carried, armed, scattered everywhere, and made to leave its tracks—not to be crushed, but to be increased. Upon them, like the most solid foundations and columns, it is raised. Whoever follows them—whether pagan, Jew, or Christian—is immediately incorporated into the Antichrist and carried by them to eternal destruction.

Then, just as the Lord Jesus is called and is the mouth of the Father, so that blasphemous one is the mouth of the roaring lion who goes about seeking whom he may devour (1 Pet. 5:8). The dragon, who is also the lion, gave him as his son and arm his own power and authority, so that he might rage throughout the world with malice both open and concealed.

But Daniel, God's initiate into the mysteries, foresaw that the heretics, incorporated into him and constituting his feet, were specially signified in another beast; John subsequently beheld them in the beast that rose from the earth and had two horns like a Lamb and spoke like a dragon.

For all heretics who claim to be Christians rise from the earth like a beast, because in the arrogance of their display or elation they come out from the solidity of the Church to serve that sea-monster—namely, the Antichrist—who swells with secular power, according to the saying of the apostle: “They went out from us, but they were not of us.”

Here “earth” may suitably be understood as the holy Church, of which the Psalmist says allegorically:

“He founded the earth upon its stability; it shall not be moved forever and ever” (Ps. 103:5).

And:

“The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the world and all who dwell in it. For he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers. Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in his holy place?” (Ps. 24:1–3.)

The Lord made her to stand above the seas—that is, above worldly pride and power. He raised her above the rivers—that is, worldly desires—so that she is now both his singular mountain and his holy place.

All who emerge from her display two horns like a Lamb, because they claim either to accept the two Testaments, or to observe the two commandments of charity, or to have their power pertain to the kingdom and priesthood of Christ, or to have been sanctified by his baptism and cross.

But in these matters they show no truth beyond the mere outward appearance of the Lamb’s horns. Hence they speak like the dragon, “who did not stand in the truth. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own nature, because he is a liar and the father of it” (John 8:44). And just as that one spoke and speaks only in order to become a murderer, so these men speak only in order to become murderers.

They also exercise all the authority of the first beast in its presence, because by concealed or open wickedness they rage against human beings no less than the Antichrist himself. Yet they do this in its presence because, just as Catholics refer to Christ whatever they do under his authorship, so heretics refer to the Antichrist whatever they do by the power given by him.

For just as the holy prophets went before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways (Luke 1:76), so these men, becoming his forerunners, go before that apostate; and whatever they do, they do in his presence. All of this can be nothing but evil, even if it appears good.

For just as the good, following the example of their Redeemer who says, “I do not seek my own glory” (John 8:50), and “I have not come to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me” (John 6:38), attribute whatever they are and can do to him, seeking not what is their own but what is Christ’s, so the reprobate, seeking only what is their own and not what is Christ’s, do whatever they do in the presence of the Antichrist (Phil. 2:21). He will come in his own name and, like a liar, speak from himself, seeking only his own glory after the example of his father, the dragon, who from the beginning sought only what was his own, when in pride he desired to establish a seat for himself and become like the Most High (Isa. 14:14).

### CHAPTER XXXIX. What are the signs and wonders of Catholics?

How heretics make the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, blessed Jerome, as was already set out above, demonstrates as follows:

“Just as idols are made by the hand of an artisan, so whoever imitates the perverse teaching of heretics turns it into an idol and causes the Antichrist to be worshiped in place of Christ.”

Because they deceive the inhabitants of the earth—namely, the Church, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave—by the signs they perform in the presence of that beast, the Lord likewise foretells this to his own in the Gospel:

“False Christs and false prophets will arise and give signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. And then, if they say to you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ,’ or, ‘There he is,’ do not believe it” (Matt. 24:23–24); do not go, nor follow them.

For just as the holy prophets before the first coming of Jesus Christ, and likewise the holy apostles and their imitators before the second, gave and give many great signs and wonders, so the heretics, whom the Lord calls false prophets and false Christs—those, so to speak, of the Antichrist—perform them before their prince, the Antichrist.

But let us inquire what signs and wonders the worshipers of Christ have given or give, and what the worshipers of the Antichrist have given or give.

Certainly, the heralds of Christ’s first coming, in all their deeds and words, placed and foreshadowed the sacraments of Christ and his Church. Thus Moses, as a figure of our supreme Pontiff, led the Israelite people across the Red Sea, fed them with manna from heaven, gave them water to drink from the rock, and purified the priests and the tabernacle with all its equipment not only with blood but also sanctified them with chrism.

This image, or shadow, of Catholic truth did not cease until Truth itself, Christ, arrived—he who is also the way and the life. Then Truth, having arisen from the earth, through the heralds of his second coming, transfers all nations through true baptism, feeds them with living and true bread, gives them new wine to drink, and continually sanctifies not only the priests but also his entire Church—first redeemed by his blood—with the anointing of his grace.

And how the Apostle carries this out, commending Christ’s bread and wine, he demonstrates: “Whenever you eat this bread and drink the cup, you will proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes” (1 Cor. 11:26).

Therefore, to say nothing for the moment about the sick who have been healed, the dead who have been brought to life, and the other benefits or punishments—which also were and are signs and wonders—let us say something about baptism alone, the sacrifice, and the anointing. These seem to us to be the principal and greatest signs and wonders, because without them no one can live for God. In these things, then, he is with us from his first coming until his second coming, which will be at the end of the age.

These are signs in such a way that they are also realities. For what they are and contain in themselves, they signify. Thus the visible baptismal font is a sign, yet it contains within itself the reality—namely, the Holy Spirit, who provides spiritual and invisible cleansing to the inner person in the mind through the bodily and visible sign displayed to the eyes of the flesh by the immersion of the outer person in water.

Understand this as referring to the sacraments of the altar; understand this also as having been said about the anointing with holy chrism. The same applies to the remaining mysteries of the Catholic Church, which are called *mysteries*, that is, “secrets,” because an unseen power is present in them. Through the visible reality, this power performs what belongs to it according to the condition and ministry of the person.

For “secret,” deriving from the verb *secerno*, means “set apart,” that is, distinguished; just as something is said to be separated from the eyes of the flesh, though not from the heart. These too are signs in such a way that they are also wonders—that is, things that speak further. For they signify the death of Christ and his past dispensation in such a way that they nonetheless now proclaim prophetically—that is, speak further—that he always lives and reigns and will come to judge the living and the dead.

## CHAPTER XL. What the Signs and Wonders of Heretics Are

[Col. 1127B]

Nevertheless, the signs and wonders before Christ’s first coming differ in this respect from the signs and wonders performed by Catholics before his second coming: the former signified in such a way that they were not realities at all, whereas the latter are signs in such a way that they are also essentially and truly realities.

It remains, therefore, to examine what the signs and wonders of that beast—which is the universal type of heretics—are, and what they signify or prophesy. Above all, it must be observed that this beast is subsequently called the false prophet. If he is a false prophet, his signs and wonders must necessarily be false. What is false must necessarily signify nothing but falsehood and a lie. It is therefore clear that no true or right sign is possessed by him who signifies nothing except false things.

But what are the signs that that beast presumes to perform for itself? They are, of course, water, bread, wine, oil, and the other visible instruments of the sacraments of the Catholic religion. These are permitted to them by God, who remains angry until the end, only as far as the eye and outward appearance are concerned, without any spiritual grace or signification.

And—would that the visible instruments of the sacraments themselves could at least be found among them in the purity of their substance or nature, and that they were free from the unclean spirit! But what is worse, they are despised by the Spirit of God and desired by the spirit of the devil, by which they are also imbued. Although outwardly there appears to be water, bread, wine, oil, and the other sacraments among them, like the food and clothing of sheep, inwardly there nevertheless lurks the savage rage of wolves.

Therefore the Lord, through Hosea, complains about the ten tribes, which bear the character of heretics, saying: “She did not know that I gave her grain, wine, and oil, and multiplied silver for her, and gold, which they made into Baal” (Hos. 2:8). And shortly afterward: “I will destroy her vine and her fig tree, and I will make it into a forest, and the beast of the field shall devour it” (ibid., 12).

By this art, then, and with these disguises, this beast makes an image of the former beast. Just as the holy fathers, through their ceremonies before the Law and under the Law, prefigured Christ who was to come, so heretics, through their sorceries, prefigure Antichrist.

For just as the mystery of eternal justice and equity—which is Christ—was then at work in our ancient fathers and is now at work in Catholics, so in heretics, as in sons of unbelief, the mystery of injustice and iniquity—which is Antichrist—is at work.

If he were not now hidden and veiled among them, the Apostle would not say concerning his manifestation: “That he may be revealed in his own time; and then that enemy will be revealed” (2 Thess. 2:8). For just as Catholics retain certain signs of the Hebrews, in which they carry and proclaim the Lord, essentially veiled, so heretics display certain appropriated signs of Catholics, in which they carry and proclaim Antichrist, veiled.
